title: Batched Pattern Search For Qaoa Parameter Optimization On Cloud-accessed Quantum Hardware
authors: Muhammad Faryad
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13669v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On a cloud-accessed quantum processor the classical optimizer of a variational algorithm communicates with the device through submitted jobs, and each job carries a queueing and turnaround overhead that does not depend on how many circuits it contains. We study a simple consequence of this for the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA). An optimizer whose next set of trial parameters is known before any result returns can evaluate the whole set in one job, whereas a sequential optimizer such as COBYLA spends one job per function evaluation. We compare a batched pattern search with COBYLA on IBM's \ibmfez\ processor for cardinality-constrained portfolio selection with six to twelve assets, giving both optimizers the same number of jobs and the same number of shots. At every size the batched search reaches, after its first job, a parameter quality that the serial optimizer takes several jobs to match, and the two methods converge to comparable final values; repeating the eight-asset comparison from four starting points gives the same ordering each time. The instances are small enough to be solved exactly, which lets us check that the device's output distribution is correlated with the true ranking of portfolios and is clearly separated from a control circuit of the same depth with the cost layer removed. A short scan over circuit depth at classically optimal parameters shows that on this device the measured solution quality peaks at two or three QAOA layers. The protocol is described in enough detail to be reproduced, and the notebooks and raw counts are released.
tldr: The paper compares a batched pattern search optimizer against COBYLA for QAOA parameter optimization on a cloud-accessed IBM quantum processor, showing job-overhead advantages for batched methods.
motivation: On cloud quantum hardware, each submitted job incurs queueing and turnaround overhead, so optimizers that require many sequential jobs can be inefficient for variational algorithms like QAOA.
method: The authors implement a batched pattern search that evaluates a set of trial parameters in a single job and compare it with the sequential COBYLA optimizer on IBM's ibm_fez processor for cardinality-constrained portfolio selection with 6–12 assets, using equal job and shot budgets.
result: The batched search reaches good parameter quality after its first job, while COBYLA takes several jobs to match, and both converge to comparable final values; the device output correlates with the true portfolio ranking and peaks at two or three QAOA layers.
conclusion: Batched optimization can reduce cloud quantum job overhead for QAOA without sacrificing final solution quality, and the protocol is fully reproducible with released notebooks and raw counts.

title: Refracted Light Interaction In Turbulent Bubbling Water (rlitbw): A Macroscopic Fluid-Optic Entropy Source
authors: Nirjhar Debnath, Dwaipayan Datta, Kousik Dasgupta
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13147v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The demand for high quality, unpredictable random numbers is a fundamental requirement in cryptography, stochastic simulation, and optimization. While pseudo-random number generators (PRNGs) are computationally efficient, their deterministic nature limits their suitability for security-critical applications. True random number generators (TRNGs), although physically grounded, often rely on expensive quantum or tightly controlled electronic phenomena. This paper introduces a low-cost, macroscopic TRNG based on Refracted Light Interaction in Turbulent Bubbling Water (RLITBW). The proposed system exploits compound classical chaos arising from multiphase fluid dynamics and time-varying optical refraction. A physical-mathematical model is developed to describe the cascade of non-linear processes from stochastic bubble nucleation and turbulent ascent to chaotic optical path scrambling that collectively amplify microscopic uncertainties into measurable entropy.The raw optical signal is digitized and processed using a provably secure entropy-conditioning pipeline based on Toeplitz universal hashing, followed by deterministic cryptographic expansion. The chaotic nature of the physical source is empirically validated using phase-space reconstruction, Lyapunov exponent estimation, autocorrelation analysis, and entropy metrics. The conditioned output successfully passes the full NIST SP 800-22 statistical test suite and nonlinear dynamical measures including Lyapunov exponents and sample entropy. Beyond statistical validation, the generated randomness is applied to population-based optimization algorithms, demonstrating practical usability as a replacement for conventional PRNGs. Finally, deployment architectures and scalability considerations are discussed, positioning RLITBW as an accessible, reproducible, and economically viable entropy source for real-world systems.
tldr: A low-cost macroscopic true random number generator is proposed that harvests entropy from refracted light interacting with turbulent bubbling water.
motivation: High-quality unpredictable random numbers are essential for cryptography and simulation, but existing true random number generators often rely on expensive quantum or tightly controlled electronic phenomena.
method: The system models compound classical chaos from stochastic bubble nucleation, turbulent ascent, and chaotic optical path scrambling, then digitizes the raw optical signal and applies Toeplitz universal hashing for entropy conditioning.
result: The conditioned output passes the full NIST SP 800-22 statistical test suite and nonlinear dynamical measures, and is demonstrated in population-based optimization algorithms.
conclusion: RLITBW offers an accessible, reproducible, and economically viable macroscopic entropy source for real-world randomness needs, though it is classical and not connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: The Price Of Locality: Maxwell-Cattaneo Charge Transport In Schwinger-Keldysh Effective Field Theory
authors: Andrea Amoretti, Matteo Anselmi, Daniel K. Brattan
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13378v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the conditions under which the nonlinear Maxwell-Cattaneo theory of charge transport admits a local Gaussian Schwinger-Keldysh embedding with a particular modified dynamical KMS symmetry. We show that treating the additional vector as intrinsically dissipative fundamentally modifies the entropy-current analysis: the hydrostatic generating functional no longer fixes all entropy-current improvements, which must instead be supplied independently. Subsequently we discuss the additional constraints not contained in the hydrodynamic analysis that are imposed by the modified KMS transformation becoming a symmetry of the action. We both interpret and supply the corresponding stochastic quasi-hydrodynamics.
tldr: The paper determines conditions for a local Gaussian Schwinger-Keldysh embedding of nonlinear Maxwell-Cattaneo charge transport with modified dynamical KMS symmetry, showing that intrinsic dissipation alters entropy-current constraints.
motivation: To understand how locality and dissipation are encoded in effective field theories for charge transport, and to clarify the role of KMS symmetry in hydrodynamic frameworks.
method: The authors employ Schwinger-Keldysh effective field theory and entropy-current analysis, treating an additional vector as intrinsically dissipative and examining constraints from a modified KMS transformation.
result: The hydrostatic generating functional no longer fixes all entropy-current improvements, which must be supplied independently; the modified KMS symmetry imposes additional constraints beyond the hydrodynamic analysis.
conclusion: The work provides an interpretation and construction of stochastic quasi-hydrodynamics for nonlinear Maxwell-Cattaneo charge transport, highlighting the price of locality in such effective descriptions.

title: Practical Considerations For Processing Massive Classical Data Via Quantum Oracle Sketching
authors: Stefano Markidis
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13549v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical-to-quantum I/O is a critical bottleneck for data-intensive quantum workloads. Quantum Oracle Sketching (QOS) has been proposed to address this problem. We identify its practical requirements, including the representation of data as a probability distribution over oracle addresses, the relation between sample count, approximation error, and update cost, and the coherence and runtime support required for online execution. To study QOS on current quantum computing devices, we develop an offline realization that compiles sample blocks into empirical phase oracles and evaluate it using DNA fingerprinting. The application converges with relatively few samples, while exact phase fusion combines repeated updates to the same address. However, the compiled circuits remain too deep for current quantum computing devices. Practical QOS therefore requires lower depth oracle synthesis and interactive quantum runtimes.
tldr: The paper studies practical requirements and an offline realization of Quantum Oracle Sketching for loading massive classical data into quantum computers, finding that current compiled circuits are too deep for existing devices.
motivation: Classical-to-quantum I/O is a critical bottleneck for data-intensive quantum workloads, and Quantum Oracle Sketching (QOS) has been proposed as a solution, but its practical requirements and feasibility on current hardware remain unclear.
method: The authors identify practical requirements of QOS, including probabilistic data representation over oracle addresses and sample-count/error/update-cost trade-offs, and develop an offline realization that compiles sample blocks into empirical phase oracles, evaluated on a DNA fingerprinting application.
result: The application converges with relatively few samples and exact phase fusion combines repeated updates, but the compiled quantum circuits remain too deep for current quantum computing devices.
conclusion: Practical QOS requires lower-depth oracle synthesis and interactive quantum runtimes before it can be deployed on near-term hardware.

title: Binary Optimization With Complex Constraints Via Quantum Approximate Multi-Objective Optimization
authors: Andres Ruiz, Soumyadip Ghosh, Stefan Woerner
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13790v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that a class of binary optimization problems with complex non-quadratic objectives or constraints can be reformulated as multi-objective quadratic unconstrained binary optimization problems. When the objective and constraints depend on a small number of quadratic features and are monotone with respect to their preferred directions, at least one globally optimal solution lies in the Pareto set of the associated MO-QUBO. This enables the constraints to be evaluated classically on Pareto-optimal candidates rather than encoded as penalties. We demonstrate the approach for binary portfolio optimization under a Conditional Value-at-Risk constraint. Using Quantum Approximate Multi-Objective Optimization on an illustrative 100-asset instance, we approximate the mean-variance Pareto front using an IBM Quantum computer and derive mean-CVaR fronts through classical post-processing. The hardware results recover the overall structure of the classical front and yield near-optimal feasible portfolios for different risk bounds.
tldr: The paper reformulates binary optimization with complex constraints as multi-objective QUBO problems and demonstrates the approach with quantum approximate multi-objective optimization on an IBM quantum computer for portfolio optimization.
motivation: Binary optimization problems with non-quadratic objectives or constraints are difficult for quantum hardware, and the authors seek to avoid penalty-term encodings by using multi-objective reformulations.
method: They show that when objectives and constraints depend on few quadratic features and are monotone, an optimal solution lies in the Pareto set of an associated MO-QUBO, allowing classical constraint evaluation; they test this with QAOA-style multi-objective optimization on a 100-asset portfolio problem.
result: Hardware results recover the overall structure of the classical Pareto front and yield near-optimal feasible portfolios for different risk bounds under a Conditional Value-at-Risk constraint.
conclusion: The multi-objective QUBO approach enables quantum-assisted binary optimization with complex constraints without penalty encoding, though the application is outside the core research interests in quantum information theory, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems.

title: Local-to-Global Isometries In Standard-Norm Generalized Gyrovector Spaces: Thompson And Hilbert Geometries Of JB-Cones
authors: Jyamira Oppekepenguin
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13620v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce standard-norm generalized gyrovector spaces: generalized gyrovector spaces whose norm-value line has the ordinary real operations and whose fixed scalar maps are continuous. We prove that every bijective gyrometric isometry between nonempty connected open subsets of two such spaces extends uniquely to a global bijective gyrometric isometry. The proof combines gyromidpoints, point reflections, continuation of local isometry germs, and monodromy; joint continuity of scalar multiplication is derived, rather than assumed. The class includes all nonzero real normed spaces and standardized M\"obius, Einstein, and proper-velocity models, and is stable under finite and countable [MATH]-products. We also obtain bounded mapping-space examples and, under natural continuity assumptions, standard-norm function-space GGVs [MATH] for compact [MATH]. These yield non-Hilbertian and hybrid examples. For every unital JB-algebra, the positive invertible cone carries a one-parameter family of standard-norm GGV structures whose gyrometrics are conjugate to Thompson's metric by power maps. The projective positive cone has a parallel family, based on the variation norm modulo the unit, conjugate to Hilbert's projective metric. The projective structures are contractible. Together with global JB-cone isometry classifications, the abstract theorem yields local-to-global extension and classification results for Thompson and Hilbert geometries. Full-rank density matrices and normalized state spaces of finite-dimensional Euclidean Jordan algebras, including the Albert algebra, give concrete projective examples.
tldr: Introduces standard-norm generalized gyrovector spaces and proves that local bijective gyrometric isometries extend globally, with applications to Thompson and Hilbert geometries on JB-cones.
motivation: To generalize local-to-global isometry results to a broad class of gyrovector spaces and to classify isometries of cones arising from Jordan algebras.
method: Combines gyromidpoints, point reflections, continuation of local isometry germs, and monodromy; joint continuity of scalar multiplication is derived rather than assumed.
result: Every bijective gyrometric isometry between connected open subsets extends uniquely; positive invertible cones of unital JB-algebras carry a one-parameter family of GGV structures conjugate to Thompson's metric, and projective positive cones have a parallel family conjugate to Hilbert's projective metric.
conclusion: The abstract theorem yields local-to-global extension and classification results for Thompson and Hilbert geometries, with concrete examples from full-rank density matrices and normalized state spaces of finite-dimensional Euclidean Jordan algebras.

title: On The Equivalence Of Stochastic Control And Path Space Formulations For Schr\"odinger Bridges Over Compact Connected Lie Groups
authors: Hamza Mahmood, Georgiy A. Bondar, Abhishek Halder, Adeel Akhtar
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13758v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the equivalence between the stochastic optimal control and path space formulations of the Schr\"odinger bridge problem (SBP) for the kinematic equation on a compact connected Lie group. Using the geometric concepts of horizontal lift and stochastic anti-development, we derive a Girsanov-type change-of-measure result, and show that the expected control energy equals the relative entropy of the controlled path law with respect to the reference Wiener measure. Thus, the SBP is equivalently a path space relative entropy minimization problem subject to prescribed endpoint marginals.Our result has three useful implications. From an analytic viewpoint, the shown equivalence helps prove the existence and uniqueness of the SB. From a probabilistic viewpoint, it helps interpret the SB as the most probable deviation of the uncontrolled stochastic dynamics consistent with the endpoint constraints. From a computational viewpoint, it allows using static Sinkhorn recursions to directly solve the relative entropy minimization problem and compute the optimal path measure. We illustrate the equivalence numerically on the torus [MATH]. The code is publicly available at: [URL].
tldr: The paper proves equivalence between stochastic optimal control and path-space relative entropy minimization formulations of the Schrödinger bridge problem on compact connected Lie groups.
motivation: Schrödinger bridges connect stochastic control and optimal transport, but their formulation on Lie groups requires geometric tools like horizontal lifts and stochastic anti-development.
method: The authors derive a Girsanov-type change of measure for the kinematic equation on a Lie group and show that expected control energy equals relative entropy of the controlled path law with respect to Wiener measure.
result: The equivalence yields existence/uniqueness of the Schrödinger bridge, a probabilistic interpretation as most probable deviation, and a computational algorithm using static Sinkhorn recursions, illustrated on the torus.
conclusion: This work unifies stochastic control and path-space formulations for Schrödinger bridges on Lie groups, enabling both theoretical analysis and practical computation via Sinkhorn iterations.

title: A Dynamic Residual Measure Of Inaccuracy Based On Varextropy
authors: Faranak Goodarzi
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a variance-based inaccuracy measure for order statistics based on the concept of varextropy. The proposed measure provides a framework for quantifying the variability of the inaccuracy function between an order statistic and its parent distribution. We establish a transformation property of the proposed measure under strictly increasing differentiable transformations. We establish theoretical upper and lower bounds for this measure. We further develop a dynamic residual version of the proposed inaccuracy measure and establish characterization results for the underlying distribution. Furthermore, we derive bounds for the dynamic residual inaccuracy measures based on extropy and varextropy. Finally, a nonparametric estimator of the proposed measure is developed and applied to real data to assess the goodness-of-fit of candidate distributions and facilitate model selection. 1.
tldr: Introduces a variance-based inaccuracy measure for order statistics using varextropy, with bounds, a dynamic residual extension, and a nonparametric estimator applied to goodness-of-fit and model selection.
motivation: Inaccuracy measures quantify divergence between distributions, and extropy/varextropy are classical alternatives to entropy; this work extends such measures to order statistics and residual/dynamic settings for reliability and statistical inference.
method: Defines a varextropy-based inaccuracy measure, derives a transformation property under increasing differentiable transformations, establishes upper and lower bounds, develops a dynamic residual version with characterization results, and constructs a nonparametric estimator.
result: The measure satisfies transformation and boundedness properties, the dynamic residual version characterizes underlying distributions, and the estimator is demonstrated on real data for goodness-of-fit assessment and model selection.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides a flexible classical statistical tool for quantifying variability in inaccuracy measures of order statistics, with potential use in reliability and applied model selection.

title: Canaries In The Bank: Auditing User-Level Privacy In Private Evolution
authors: Sai Aparna Aketi, Enayat Ullah, Shripad Gade
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13499v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Private Evolution (PE) generates high-fidelity synthetic data in federated settings without exposing users' raw data. It aggregates clipped user votes over a shared candidate bank into a differentially private histogram, with noise calibrated to the worst-case user contribution. However, it is unclear whether an adversary can realize this worst-case privacy loss while following the PE protocol. We introduce a protocol-aware empirical audit in which the server commits to a single shared candidate bank and replaces roughly 1% of its entries with probes derived from a known, non-private canary. We evaluate eight attacks, including an unchanged-bank baseline, exact copies, plausible paraphrases, and high-entropy synthetic nonces. Experiments on Yelp and Sentiment140 show that natural-text attacks remain substantially below the theoretical DP bound, while nonce-based attacks yield considerably stronger bounds and come closest to the mechanism's privacy ceiling. These results quantify the gap between formal worst-case privacy and leakage achievable through protocol-valid candidate-bank manipulation.
tldr: This paper empirically audits user-level privacy in Private Evolution, showing a gap between theoretical differential privacy bounds and protocol-valid leakage.
motivation: Private Evolution provides differentially private synthetic data in federated settings, but it is unclear whether the formal worst-case privacy loss can be realized by an adversary following the protocol.
method: The authors introduce a protocol-aware empirical audit where the server inserts canary-derived probes into about 1% of a shared candidate bank and evaluate eight attacks on Yelp and Sentiment140.
result: Natural-text attacks remain below theoretical DP bounds, while nonce-based attacks yield stronger bounds and approach the mechanism's privacy ceiling.
conclusion: Protocol-valid candidate-bank manipulation can achieve leakage closer to the worst-case bound than natural-text attacks, quantifying the gap between formal privacy and practical auditing.

title: Positive Topology And Feasible Refinement: Forcing Matrices, Positivity, And Information
authors: Giovanni Sambin Mirco A. Mannucci
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13523v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a conceptual and operational account of Positive Topology starting from a basic relation between points or models and observable properties. From this relation, two complementary structures emerge. The first captures universal refinement and cover: what must hold across all relevant cases and how information can be systematically refined. The second captures positivity and witnessed existence: what can be positively realized and sustained without relying on classical complements. A central result shows that the underlying relation between points and observables can be reconstructed from either of these induced structures. We also clarify the distinction between point-based and pointfree formulations: when points are available, positivity can be derived from the underlying forcing relation, while in the formal pointfree setting positivity is taken as primitive and its compatibility with cover is imposed axiomatically. We develop two complementary interpretations of the framework. The first is information-theoretic, viewing cover as refinement of partial information and positivity as witnessed feasibility. The second is game-theoretic, viewing positivity as the ability of a witness or hypothesis to survive successive legitimate refinements. The final part of the paper is deliberately programmatic. We outline how resource constraints, verification costs, and finite budgets can be incorporated into the framework. This leads to resource-sensitive notions of forcing, cover, positivity, and refinement, and raises new questions about how these structures behave as available resources change. Examples from medical diagnosis, legal reasoning, and AI systems illustrate the potential relevance of the approach to grounded, explainable, and resource-aware inference.
tldr: The paper develops a conceptual and operational framework called Positive Topology, based on a primitive relation between points and observable properties, with complementary structures for universal refinement/cover and for positivity/witnessed existence, and sketches resource-sensitive extensions.
motivation: The authors aim to give a constructive, pointfree account of topology and information refinement that avoids classical complements, motivated by applications in medical diagnosis, legal reasoning, and explainable resource-aware AI inference.
method: They introduce a basic point-observable relation, derive cover and positivity structures from it, show each structure can reconstruct the other, contrast point-based and pointfree formulations with forcing relations, and offer information-theoretic and game-theoretic readings before outlining resource-constrained forcing and refinement.
result: A central result shows the underlying point-observable relation is recoverable from either induced structure; positivity follows from forcing when points exist and is taken as primitive axiomatically in the pointfree setting, with compatibility with cover imposed by axiom.
conclusion: The framework is deliberately programmatic, proposing resource-sensitive notions of forcing, cover, positivity, and refinement and raising open questions about how these structures behave as budgets and verification costs vary.

title: Formulating Multistage Cutting Stock Problems As Qubo
authors: Marcel Seelbach Benkner, Chiara Capecci, Sebastian Nagies, Javed Akram, Sebastian Rubbert, Dimitrios Bantounas, Philipp Hauke, Michael Johanning, Michael Moeller
abstract: ArXiv:2609.14070v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cutting stock problems are of large relevance to a variety of industry branches. Here, we present a linear programming formulation for a restricted version of the multistage 2D cutting stock problem with Guillotine cuts and test it on published benchmark instances. After this, we derive a non-exact reformulation in quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) form via unbalanced penalization, which we show to have possible benefits in modeling the problem with usable leftovers. This work mainly considers the restricted formulation, in which the dimensions of each cut are determined by those of a single required piece. We further discuss how the approach can be extended to the unrestricted problem, which allows more general cutting patterns involving cuts with dimensions of multiple required pieces and naturally gives rise to quadratic terms in the inequalities of the problem formulation. We showcase solutions via a Simulated Annealing solver for the restricted problem class, where we mainly study the performance of the iterative augmented Lagrangian method. We also discuss possible applications of Quantum Annealing in this setting, as a strong motivation to research QUBO formulations.
tldr: The paper formulates restricted multistage 2D cutting stock problems as QUBO and benchmarks simulated annealing and augmented Lagrangian methods, with brief discussion of quantum annealing.
motivation: Cutting stock problems are industrially important, and QUBO formulations could enable quantum annealing or other Ising solvers to tackle such combinatorial optimization tasks.
method: The authors present a linear programming formulation for a restricted 2D guillotine cutting stock problem, then derive a non-exact QUBO reformulation via unbalanced penalization and solve it with simulated annealing and an iterative augmented Lagrangian method.
result: They test the approach on published benchmark instances and show potential benefits in modeling problems with usable leftovers, while extending ideas toward unrestricted cutting patterns that introduce quadratic terms.
conclusion: The work mainly provides a QUBO-based optimization formulation and classical solver study, with quantum annealing discussed as future motivation rather than a demonstrated quantum advantage.

title: Versatile Sleeve-and-Bulk Fabrication Of Inversely Designed Nanophotonic Structures With High Pattern Transfer Fidelity
authors: Lan Hoang Mai, Radheya Sham Sarode, William G. Eshbaugh, Sulaiman Al Ghadani, Tyler Manfre, Nazifa Tasnim Arony, Joshua M. O. Zide, Matthew F. Doty, Edward B. Flagg
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13460v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inverse design is a powerful computational tool for generating nanophotonic devices that should outperform their traditionally designed counterparts. However, translating these theoretical gains into physical devices is challenging because the irregular and non-intuitive features that make inversely designed structures so effective also make them exceptionally difficult to fabricate, typically necessitating substantial process optimization unique to each device design. We describe a versatile two-step nanofabrication process that achieves pattern transfer fidelity in excess of 90% for each of three distinct inverse device designs with no device-specific process optimization.
tldr: A two-step nanofabrication process achieving over 90% pattern transfer fidelity for three distinct inversely designed nanophotonic structures without device-specific process optimization.
motivation: Inverse design yields nanophotonic devices with superior theoretical performance, but the irregular, non-intuitive geometries are hard to fabricate, usually requiring extensive per-device process tuning.
method: The authors develop a versatile 'sleeve-and-bulk' two-step lithographic fabrication approach and apply it to three different inverse-designed device layouts, measuring pattern transfer fidelity for each.
result: Pattern transfer fidelity exceeding 90% was achieved for all three distinct inverse device designs, with no device-specific process optimization required.
conclusion: The approach offers a general, design-agnostic fabrication route that helps translate inverse-designed nanophotonic performance gains into physical devices.

title: Transverse-Anderson Localization Of Light In Disordered Silicon Pores
authors: S. Erfanifam, C. Yanik, M. Erfanifam
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13484v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transverse light localization of Anderson type through disorders has made intriguing fundamental topics. Toward this, we found that in the disordered porous Si (PSi) a nearly "zero reflection" (from 450 to 900 nm) can be observed. The localization length versus disorder parameter is experimentally visualized and calculated based on a self consistent theory and solution of stochastic Helmholtz equation for electric fields traveling in a transverse disordered media with the results determined to be in a reasonable agreement with experiments. Based on these calculations for different pore diameters in a constant order parameter, diffusion length can vary from 260 nm to 2.4\mu m, accounting as controllability of such structure for further applications in photonic devices. Reflection from ordered PSi structure are evaluated that shows no similar responses to those seen in disordered PSi.
tldr: The paper experimentally and theoretically studies transverse Anderson localization of light in disordered porous silicon, mapping localization/diffusion lengths versus disorder and pore diameter.
motivation: Anderson-type transverse light localization is a fundamental wave-physics phenomenon, and disordered porous Si offers a tunable platform to explore it with potential photonic device applications.
method: Reflection and localization measurements on disordered versus ordered porous Si from 450 to 900 nm, combined with a self-consistent theory and stochastic Helmholtz equation solutions for electric fields in transverse disordered media.
result: Near-zero reflection is observed over 450–900 nm in disordered PSi, with calculated diffusion lengths tunable from 260 nm to 2.4 µm across pore diameters, in reasonable agreement with experiment; ordered PSi shows no comparable response.
conclusion: Disordered porous silicon provides controllable transverse Anderson localization of light, suggesting its use as a tunable element in photonic devices.

title: What Output-Equivalence Oracles Miss: An Empirical Study Of Equivalence-Invisible Bug Fixes In Quantum Transpilers (Qiskit, Tket, Cirq)
authors: Furqan Nasir, Arif Shah, Iftikhar Alam
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13839v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum compilers are judged correct by an output-equivalence oracle: the compiled circuit must compute the same unitary as the original, modulo global phase and a qubit-layout permutation. This oracle, by construction, checks only that semantic map, not the circuit's own layout, permutation, or phase records: a defect there, or in a fixed-seed run's determinism, can pass unseen though the record is public. We measure how often this happens in real merged compiler fixes: a systematically identified corpus of Qiskit transpiler bug-fixes, classified by an independently dual-coded, source-validated manifestation taxonomy. Nineteen of 68 fixes (28%, 95% Wilson CI 19-40%) repair faults that this equivalence screen does not catch, even one augmented with compilation-validity, circuit-quality, and performance checks. A secondary wider-window robustness sample produced a nearly identical fraction (29/104, 27.9%, CI 20-37%). A conservative floor remains even restricted to the one unconditionally equivalence-invisible channel (a corrupted layout or permutation record): 10 of 68 fixes (15%, CI 8-25%) beneath the 28% headline. The gap is not Qiskit-specific: it replicates in tket (7 of 21, 33%), with Cirq smaller but consistent. We detected no systematic differences on five inexpensive PR-level characteristics (19 vs 49, underpowered to rule out a modest true difference). This class dominates the invisible set, concentrating at representation-boundary crossings. We release the corpus, codebook, and coding artifacts. Here we only measure it.
tldr: An empirical study finds that many merged bug fixes in quantum transpilers (Qiskit, tket, Cirq) repair faults that standard output-equivalence oracles fail to detect, especially layout, permutation, phase-record, and determinism issues.
motivation: Quantum compilers are typically validated by an output-equivalence oracle that only checks unitary equivalence modulo global phase and qubit permutation, ignoring circuit metadata such as layout, permutation, phase records, and fixed-seed determinism, so some real defects may pass unseen.
method: The authors systematically identify a corpus of Qiskit transpiler bug-fixes, classify them with a dual-coded source-validated taxonomy, and check whether an output-equivalence oracle—augmented with compilation-validity, circuit-quality, and performance checks—would catch each fix; they replicate the analysis in tket and Cirq.
result: Nineteen of 68 Qiskit fixes (28%, 95% Wilson CI 19–40%) are equivalence-invisible, with a conservative floor of 10/68 (15%, CI 8–25%) for corrupted layout or permutation records alone; the gap replicates in tket (7/21, 33%) and is consistent though smaller in Cirq.
conclusion: Output-equivalence oracles miss a substantial and systematic class of real quantum transpiler bugs that concentrate at representation-boundary crossings, motivating broader verification beyond unitary equivalence; the authors release the corpus, codebook, and coding artifacts.

title: Vortex Solitons In Star Networks
authors: Yaroslav V. Kartashov
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13951v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: I consider vortex solitons in two-dimensional star networks created by several one-dimensional line waveguide arrays (or rays) brought in close proximity. First waveguide in each array belongs to the ring of certain radius and its modal field overlaps with modal fields of waveguides from other rays laying on this ring, as well as with modal fields of waveguides in this line array. This creates a system with discrete rotational symmetry that is capable of supporting various localized linear vortex states due to local coupling between waveguides on the central ring, where line arrays approach each other. Localized vortex states emerge from the continuum of the states extended along the rays of the structure upon variation of the radius of the central ring. I show how different vortex modes with progressively increasing topological charges emerge when the number of rays in structure and, therefore, its discrete rotational symmetry increases. Each such linear localized mode gives rise to a family of thresholdless vortex solitons in nonlinear optical medium, whose topological charges are limited by the discrete rotational symmetry of the system. Vortex solitons in star networks exhibit qualitatively different behavior with increasing power depending on whether the propagation constant of linear vortex that gives rise to a family of solitons is located above or below the band of extended states. Stability properties of vortex solitons nontrivially depend on their topological charge and discrete rotational symmetry of the system, showing very different picture from usual ring-like waveguide arrays.
tldr: Theoretical study of vortex solitons in two-dimensional star networks formed by line waveguide arrays with discrete rotational symmetry.
motivation: To explore localized vortex states and thresholdless soliton families in nonlinear optical star networks, revealing how discrete rotational symmetry controls topological charge.
method: Analyzes linear localized vortex modes arising from coupling on a central ring of coupled waveguides, then studies nonlinear vortex solitons in a Kerr medium.
result: Shows that localized vortex modes with increasing topological charge emerge as the number of rays increases, and each gives rise to a family of thresholdless vortex solitons whose stability depends on the propagation constant relative to the band of extended states.
conclusion: Vortex solitons in star networks exhibit qualitatively different behavior from those in usual ring-like waveguide arrays, with stability nontrivially dependent on topological charge and discrete rotational symmetry.

title: Conditional Quantum Flow Matching For Data-Scarce Physiological Signal Augmentation
authors: Samuel Yen-Chi Chen Chi-Sheng Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.14019v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative augmentation is a standard remedy for label scarcity in physiological signal classification, but existing quantum generative models start from uninformative noise, ignoring class structure that is already available. We propose Conditional Quantum Flow Matching (CQFM): a single 306-parameter circuit, conditioned on both flow time and class label, transports a compact class-conditional prior toward the target distribution. Quantum flow matching as published is unconditional, so this is to our knowledge the first conditional one, and the first EEG augmentation on a parameterized quantum circuit. A nonnegative spectral embedding removes the need for tomography at readout. On BCI Competition IV-2a, starting from a prior rather than noise is worth [MATH] accuracy points over QuDDPM (9/9 subjects), though at that operating point a class-conditional Gaussian matches CQFM. Where the prior fails the transport earns its keep: given one transferred from other subjects it regains [MATH] TSTR points (9/9).
tldr: The paper introduces Conditional Quantum Flow Matching (CQFM), the first class-conditional quantum flow-matching generative model, applied to augment scarce EEG data for physiological signal classification.
motivation: Label scarcity hampers physiological signal classification, and existing quantum generative augmentation models (e.g., QuDDPM) start from uninformative noise, discarding useful class structure; the authors aim to exploit a class-conditional prior instead.
method: A single 306-parameter parameterized quantum circuit is conditioned on both flow time and class label to transport a compact class-conditional prior to the target distribution, with a nonnegative spectral embedding that avoids tomography at readout.
result: On BCI Competition IV-2a, using a prior rather than noise yields gains over QuDDPM for 9/9 subjects, though a class-conditional Gaussian matches CQFM at that operating point; when a prior transferred from other subjects fails, the transport recovers TSTR points for 9/9 subjects.
conclusion: Conditional quantum flow matching offers a viable data-scarce augmentation route for EEG, with the transport mechanism providing the most value when the supplied prior is imperfect.

title: When Do Pilots Matter For Ofdm Sensing? Pilot-Data Resource Design For Isac
authors: Shengcai Zhou, Luping Xiang, Yi Wang, Kun Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13329v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Practical OFDM-based integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) signals contain deterministic pilots and random data payloads, yet how these two types of resources jointly affect matched-filter sensing performance remains insufficiently understood. This paper establishes an analytical and optimization framework for pilot-data (P-D) OFDM sensing. We first derive a closed-form mean-square periodic autocorrelation function (MS P-ACF), which characterizes the respective contributions of the average subcarrier power spectrum and data-symbol randomness to sensing sidelobes. Based on this result, we reveal that pilot placement has no impact on normalized sidelobes under uniform power allocation or on the normalized global expected integrated sidelobe level (EISL), whereas it becomes an effective design degree of freedom for reshaping sidelobes under nonuniform power allocation. We further derive the globally optimal two-level pilot-data power allocation for global EISL minimization and characterize pilot placement for peak sidelobe suppression. For region-of-interest (ROI) sensing, we jointly optimize pilot placement and subcarrier power allocation to minimize the normalized ROI-EISL. A strictly uniform pilot placement is proved globally optimal under specified conditions, while a bisection-and-branch-and-bound algorithm is developed for general resource configurations. Numerical results validate the theoretical analysis and demonstrate that the proposed design reduces the ROI sidelobe level by up to 2.19 dB compared with optimized uniform-pilot OFDM, while improving ranging accuracy at an SNR of -10 dB by 84.3[MATH]. These results reveal when and how pilot placement can be exploited to regulate the sensing behavior of random OFDM communication signals, providing practical resource-design principles for OFDM-based ISAC.
tldr: The paper develops an analytical and optimization framework for pilot-data resource design in OFDM-based integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), characterizing how pilot placement and subcarrier power allocation affect matched-filter sensing sidelobes.
motivation: Practical OFDM ISAC waveforms contain deterministic pilots and random data payloads, but how these two resource types jointly influence sensing performance via the matched filter was not well understood.
method: The authors derive a closed-form mean-square periodic autocorrelation function (MS P-ACF) capturing power-spectrum and data-randomness contributions to sidelobes, then optimize pilot placement and two-level power allocation for global EISL, peak sidelobe, and region-of-interest EISL, using bisection and branch-and-bound algorithms.
result: Pilot placement is shown to be irrelevant under uniform power allocation but becomes a design lever under nonuniform allocation; the proposed design reduces ROI sidelobe level by up to 2.19 dB versus optimized uniform-pilot OFDM and improves ranging accuracy by 84.3% at SNR = -10 dB.
conclusion: The work clarifies when and how pilot placement can regulate sensing behavior of random OFDM communication signals, offering practical resource-design principles for OFDM-based ISAC.

title: Worse Routes, Fresher Information: Preemption Redefines Which Route Is Best
authors: Adem Utku Atasayar, Aimin Li, Elif Uysal
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13622v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies joint sampling, route activation, and preemption control over [MATH] heterogeneous transmission routes under a long-run objective combining Age of Information (AoI) with sampling and transmission costs. We formulate the problem as an average-cost impulse-control model, derive a vector-form integral average-cost optimality equation over a hybrid state space, and establish structural reductions on the state. We consider a two-route case and compute optimized policies using discretized policy iteration. Surprisingly, the results show that preemption can reverse routing preferences: the optimized policy may exclusively use a route with both a larger mean delay and a larger delay variance while avoiding the seemingly superior route. Relative to baselines that do not allow preemption, the proposed policy reduces average AoI by up to [MATH].
tldr: The paper studies joint sampling, route activation, and preemption control for Age of Information minimization over heterogeneous transmission routes, showing preemption can reverse optimal routing preferences.
motivation: Age of Information is important for timely status updates in communication networks, but the interplay between routing, sampling, and preemption under long-run cost objectives is not well understood.
method: The problem is formulated as an average-cost impulse-control model over a hybrid state space, with structural reductions and discretized policy iteration used for computation in a two-route case.
result: Optimized policies with preemption can exclusively use a route with both larger mean delay and larger delay variance, avoiding the seemingly better route, and reduce average AoI by up to a reported margin relative to non-preemptive baselines.
conclusion: Preemption fundamentally redefines which transmission route is best, highlighting counterintuitive routing behavior in freshness-oriented networked systems.

title: Convergence Of Random Products Of Projections Under Infinite-Periodic Selections

title: A Novel Approach To Counterexamples Of The Polujan-Pott Conjecture Via Set-Partition Permutations
authors: Yansheng Wu, Jiaxin Wang, Jong Yoon Hyun
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13968v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we settle a conjecture of Polujan and Pott by constructing an explicit, infinite family of Maiorana--McFarland bent functions [MATH] in [MATH] variables with algebraic degree [MATH] for any integer [MATH]. motivation: The Polujan–Pott conjecture concerned the existence of bent functions of a particular algebraic degree; settling it clarifies structural limits on bent functions, which are central objects in classical Boolean function theory and related to difference sets and designs.
method: The authors construct a minimal commutative algebra inducing a triangular set-partition polynomial permutation, identify an elementary abelian subgroup in a direct sum, and use an explicit nonlinear coordinate transformation to pull the bent function back to a canonical quadratic form, linearizing the translation development.
result: They obtain an infinite family of n-variable Maiorana–McFarland bent functions with the conjectured algebraic degree and prove the corresponding translation development is isomorphic to the classical symplectic design.

title: Programming Spintronic Reservoir Computing
authors: Yuichiro Terasaki, Yusuke Imai, Jason Z. Kim, Kohei Nakajima
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13169v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a programming framework for a spintronic reservoir computer (RC) that maps prescribed input-output relationships directly onto the readout layer, bypassing conventional data-driven black-box approaches. Our spintronic RC is based on magnetoresistive random-access memory and exploits magnetization dynamics for computation. We introduce a general metric that quantifies the system's programmability and reveals how the governing equations and system parameters constrain the class of realizable functions. We then construct externally controllable readout layers by exploiting the explicit parameter dependence of the prescribed equations. This metric and construction enable programming explicit functions on the spintronic RC, indicating a potential route to in-memory computing. Our demonstrations include neural-network emulation, bifurcation embedding, and a Newton solver for fifth-order algebraic equations. In addition, we prove the universal approximation property of the spintronic RC in the limit of infinite system size and input duration, and show its consistency with programmability.
tldr: The paper introduces a programming framework for a spintronic reservoir computer based on magnetoresistive random-access memory, enabling direct mapping of input-output relationships onto an externally controllable readout layer.
motivation: Conventional reservoir computing relies on black-box training, which limits interpretability and programmability for in-memory computing applications. The authors aim to program explicit functions in spintronic hardware.
method: They define a programmability metric and construct externally controllable readout layers by exploiting the governing equations' parameter dependence, using magnetization dynamics in MRAM for computation.
result: They demonstrate neural-network emulation, bifurcation embedding, and a Newton solver for fifth-order algebraic equations, and prove universal approximation in the limit of infinite system size and input duration.
conclusion: The work shows a potential route to programmable in-memory computing with spintronic reservoir computers, though it is a classical neuromorphic computing paper with no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Qc-ccg: Quantum-Classical Algorithm For Two-stage Adaptive Robust Optimization
authors: Duong The Do, Jiaming Cheng, Duong Tung Nguyen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13216v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum optimization provides a promising approach for solving large-scale combinatorial problems through quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) formulations. However, integrating QUBO-based solvers into structured optimization frameworks while preserving solution guarantees remains a fundamental challenge. This paper develops a hybrid quantum-classical column-and-constraint generation (QCCG) framework for solving two-stage adaptive robust optimization problems with binary first-stage decisions and linear recourse under polyhedral uncertainty. The proposed approach reformulates the restricted master problem as a QUBO and solves it approximately using a quantum optimizer, while retaining a classical adversarial subproblem to compute worst-case recourse and certify solution quality. We construct a constraint-preserving QUBO encoding for inequality-constrained master problems using slack variables and penalty terms, enabling general mixed-integer structures to be mapped to quantum-compatible representations. To address inexactness arising from discretization, penalty modeling, and quantum optimization, we introduce a bound-adjustment mechanism that yields valid lower and upper bounds and provides a certified stopping criterion. We show that the proposed framework generalizes classical column-and-constraint generation and retains its convergence properties when the master problem is solved exactly. Numerical experiments on two-stage robust location-transportation problems demonstrate that the proposed hybrid approach achieves solution quality comparable to classical methods while reducing the computational burden associated with solving mixed-integer master problems, highlighting the potential of hybrid quantum-classical optimization for scalable decision-making under uncertainty.
tldr: The paper develops a hybrid quantum-classical column-and-constraint generation framework for two-stage adaptive robust optimization using QUBO formulations and a quantum optimizer.
motivation: Quantum optimization via QUBO is promising for large combinatorial problems, but integrating QUBO solvers into structured optimization frameworks while preserving solution guarantees remains challenging.
method: The restricted master problem is reformulated as a QUBO with slack variables and penalty terms and solved approximately with a quantum optimizer, while a classical adversarial subproblem computes worst-case recourse and a bound-adjustment mechanism certifies solution quality.
result: Numerical experiments on two-stage robust location-transportation problems show solution quality comparable to classical methods while reducing the computational burden of solving mixed-integer master problems.
conclusion: The proposed hybrid quantum-classical approach generalizes classical column-and-constraint generation and highlights the potential of quantum optimization for scalable decision-making under uncertainty.

title: Perturbation Equivalence In Labelled Markov Chains
authors: Syyeda Zainab Fatmi, Stefan Kiefer, James C. A. Main, David Parker
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13401v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Behavioural equivalences, such as language equivalence and probabilistic bisimilarity, are fundamental techniques for reducing the size of probabilistic models. However, these equivalences are sensitive to the precise values of transition probabilities, making them unsuitable in applications where probabilities are subject to approximation. Motivated by settings in which the support graph of a labelled Markov chain is known but the transition probabilities are uncertain, we study robust variants of these equivalences. We introduce universal (perturbation) equivalence, which captures a variant of equivalence that is resilient to all perturbations of transition probabilities: two states or distributions are universally equivalent if they remain equivalent under every assignment of transition probabilities consistent with the support graph. We also consider the dual notion of existential (perturbation) equivalence, which holds whenever there exists an assignment of transition probabilities that yields equivalence. We establish that, for states, universal language equivalence coincides with universal probabilistic bisimilarity and develop a characterisation that yields a polynomial-time partition refinement algorithm. We implement the algorithm and demonstrate experimentally that it is effective as a technique for robust model reduction. We further show that universal language equivalence for distributions is closely related to the state case, and prove NL-completeness of deciding universal equivalence for both states and distributions. We prove that, for states, existential language equivalence coincides with existential probabilistic bisimilarity and deterministic witness transition functions always suffice, leading to an NP-completeness result. In contrast, we show that existential language equivalence for distributions is complete for the existential theory of the reals.
tldr: The paper introduces universal and existential perturbation equivalences for labelled Markov chains, characterizes them, and studies their computational complexity and use in robust model reduction.
motivation: Classical behavioural equivalences for probabilistic models are sensitive to exact transition probabilities, making them unsuitable when probabilities are uncertain but the support graph is known.
method: The authors define universal and existential perturbation equivalence, prove characterizations relating them to probabilistic bisimilarity, develop a polynomial-time partition refinement algorithm for states, and analyze complexity for distributions.
result: For states, universal language equivalence coincides with universal probabilistic bisimilarity and is decidable in polynomial time, while deciding universal equivalence for states and distributions is NL-complete; existential state equivalence is NP-complete, and existential distribution equivalence is complete for the existential theory of the reals.
conclusion: Perturbation-robust equivalences provide a foundation for robust model reduction of labelled Markov chains and reveal a rich complexity landscape depending on states versus distributions and universal versus existential semantics.

title: Basis Rigidity Of The Aes S-box And Generic Rigidity Of Inversion Under Affine Transformations
authors: Na Zhang Zheng Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13644v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The AES S-box is constructed from finite field inversion followed by a fixed affine transformation. Since inversion possesses intrinsic Frobenius symmetries among its coordinate realizations, we study how these basis symmetries are altered by outer affine transformations. We first develop a deterministic rigidity criterion for transformed inversion and apply it to the AES S-box. This shows that the linear part of the AES S-box affine transformation alone makes the transformed inversion map basis rigid. We then investigate the corresponding generic problem when the outer invertible linear transformation varies. The existence of a nontrivial linear stabilizer is reduced to a conjugacy problem for semilinear candidates arising from two sided linear equivalences of inversion, which we characterize in terms of relative norms and Frobenius orbits. We also determine the dimensions of the associated centralizer algebras exactly. These structural results imply that, for a uniformly chosen outer linear transformation, the probability that the linear stabilizer is nontrivial is bounded by [MATH], with sharper finite dimensional bounds obtained from the exact conjugacy condition. Computational experiments independently verify the AES rigidity result, the conjugacy and centralizer formulas, and the finite dimensional estimates in small dimensions.

motivation: The AES S-box is built from finite-field inversion plus an affine transformation, and its Frobenius symmetries motivate understanding how outer affine transformations affect basis rigidity.
method: The authors develop a deterministic rigidity criterion for transformed inversion and reduce the existence of nontrivial linear stabilizers to a conjugacy problem for semilinear candidates, characterized via relative norms and Frobenius orbits.
result: They prove that the AES S-box's affine transformation makes the transformed inversion basis rigid, derive exact centralizer-algebra dimensions, and bound the probability of nontrivial stabilizers for random outer linear transformations.
conclusion: The work provides structural algebraic results for AES-like inversion maps and verifies them computationally, but it lies outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Stochastic Model Of Intracellular Calcium Concentrations
authors: Tom\'as Caraballo, Macarena G\'omez-M\'armol, Ignacio Rold\'an
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13213v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study a slow-fast model of Intracellular Calcium Concentrations (ICC) within a stochastic framework, where stochastic perturbations are introduced to capture the intrinsic randomness of such biological systems. We first analyse the three-dimensional single-cell model, based on the FitzHugh-Nagumo structure, and subsequently extend the analysis to a coupled two-cell six-dimensional setting. We prove existence and uniqueness of solutions and establish positivity of the calcium variable. We obtain explicit mean-square stability estimates around deterministic equilibria and quantify how they depend on the noise intensity. Numerical simulations for both the single-cell and coupled systems illustrate relevant qualitative behaviours and reveal additional dynamical features arising in the stochastic framework.
tldr: The paper develops and analyzes a stochastic slow-fast model of intracellular calcium concentrations for single-cell and coupled two-cell systems.
motivation: Intracellular calcium dynamics are inherently noisy biological processes, motivating a stochastic framework to capture intrinsic randomness and study stability around deterministic equilibria.
method: The authors formulate a three-dimensional FitzHugh-Nagumo-type single-cell model and extend it to a six-dimensional coupled two-cell system with stochastic perturbations, proving existence, uniqueness, and positivity, and deriving mean-square stability estimates.
result: They obtain explicit mean-square stability bounds depending on noise intensity and illustrate qualitative dynamical behaviors via numerical simulations for both single-cell and coupled systems.
conclusion: The stochastic framework provides stability estimates and reveals additional dynamical features beyond deterministic models, but the work is biological and does not connect to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Matching Higher-Order Oracle Complexity For Smooth Monotone Variational Inequalities

title: Global Convergence Of An Efficient Splitting Method For The Defocusing Gross--Pitaevskii Ground State Problem
authors: Jiaxing Li, Shixin Zheng, Xiangxiong Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13509v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For computing the ground state of the defocusing Gross--Pitaevskii energy, we propose and analyze two efficient schemes based on the Davis--Yin three-operator splitting, which treats the potential and interaction terms explicitly, and the kinetic energy by a resolvent. One iteration costs one inversion of [MATH] for the first scheme, and of [MATH] for the second, with [MATH] denoting the separable part of the potential, and on structured meshes both operators can be inverted by simple fast GPU solvers. For monotone discrete Laplacians, including the second-order finite difference scheme and the lumped linear finite element method on simplicial meshes with suitable angle conditions, we prove global convergence to the unique positive discrete ground state, for every positive normalized initial vector, for any constant step size below an explicit threshold. motivation: Ground-state computation for the defocusing Gross-Pitaevskii equation is numerically challenging because previously globally convergent methods require inverting an elliptic operator that depends on the iteration variable, making each step costly.
method: Two splitting schemes based on Davis-Yin three-operator splitting treat the potential and interaction terms explicitly while handling the kinetic energy via a resolvent, requiring only inversion of separable/Laplacian-type operators that admit fast GPU solvers on structured meshes.

title: The Generalized Excursion Coupling As The Limit Of Concave Optimal Transport
authors: Yash Kanoria
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13587v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Monge-Kantorovich problem with the Euclidean distance cost is degenerate, typically admitting infinitely many optimal plans. A unique optimal plan is selected by perturbing the distance to a strictly convex or increasing strictly concave cost and passing to the limit: the convex side gives the plan induced by the map which is monotone on each transport ray, while the concave side was understood only on the real line, where Juillet proved that power-cost optimizers converge to the so-called excursion coupling, which is induced by a map when the source is atomless. This paper extends the concave selection to [MATH] for mutually singular finite positive Borel measures [MATH] and [MATH] with equal total mass and finite first moments, assuming that [MATH] is absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure: for a broad class of increasing strictly concave perturbations of the distance with a well-defined first-order profile, the corresponding optimal maps converge in [MATH]-measure to the same intrinsic limit [MATH], independent of the perturbation family and its profile. The map [MATH] is obtained by disintegrating the transport along its maximal rays and applying the one-dimensional excursion coupling on each ray. The same limit is established for the power costs [MATH] under a finite [MATH] moment condition, establishing a conjecture of Juillet.

motivation: The Monge-Kantorovich problem with Euclidean distance cost is degenerate and admits infinitely many optimal plans; while convex perturbations select a unique plan via monotone maps, the concave side was only understood on the real line, motivating its extension to higher dimensions and general measures.
method: Using disintegration of transport along maximal rays and applying the one-dimensional excursion coupling on each ray, the author establishes convergence in measure for optimal maps associated with concave perturbations and power costs under finite moment conditions.
result: For absolutely continuous source measure and mutually singular finite positive Borel measures with equal mass and finite first moments, the optimal maps converge to the same intrinsic limit independent of the perturbation family and its profile, confirming Juillet's conjecture for power costs.
conclusion: The generalized excursion coupling provides a universal concave limit for optimal transport in higher dimensions, completing the picture for degenerate Euclidean cost selection.

title: Isomorphisms And Slow Entropy Of Deterministic $[t,t^{-1}]$ Systems
authors: Nicanor Carrasco-Vargas
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13589v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study skew product measure-preserving systems driven by an irrational rotation and the step function with values [MATH] and [MATH] on each half of the circle. These systems can be seen as a deterministic version of the [MATH] system, and are particular instances of Rokhlin cocycle extensions. Under the assumption of ergodicity, we show that these systems obey an interesting rigidity property, in the sense that only obvious isomorphisms are possible. We prove that two skew products are isomorphic if and only if the rotations in the base are isomorphic, and the fiber transformations are flip isomorphic. Under mild extra assumptions, we are able to fully characterize all possible isomorphism maps. We prove that by choosing the rotation angle in the base suitably, these skew products can realize arbitrarily low measure-theoretic complexity in the sense of lower slow entropy. We apply this result to obtain new examples of systems that fail the variational principle for slow entropy. These examples can have a set of invariant measures as rich as desired (any metrizable Choquet simplex, up to affine homeomorphism).

motivation: The work aims to understand the classification and complexity of deterministic analogues of [t,t^{-1}] systems as Rokhlin cocycle extensions.
