conclusion: These results provide rigid classification and show that deterministic [t,t^{-1}] systems can exhibit rich invariant-measure simplices while having arbitrarily low complexity.

title: Feasibility And Memory Mechanisms Of Chern-Simons Context Reservoir Computation
authors: Venkatesh H. Chembrolu Jyotiranjan Beuria
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate whether a Chern-Simons (CS) context reservoir is a viable computational substrate and whether evolving its gauge connection provides a benefit beyond simpler mechanisms. The reservoir state is a density fluctuation on a two-dimensional context manifold, whose drift is generated by a density-sourced connection. To separate generic reservoir behavior from gauge-specific effects, we compare four matched models: reciprocal transport, instantaneous transverse reconstruction, local nonlinear feedback, and fully coupled conserved-current CS dynamics. Across ten random seeds, the fully coupled CS dynamics propagates Gauss law to numerical precision, converges under spatial and temporal refinement, remains stable under constraint-compatible noise, and satisfies the spatial CS equation more accurately than the instantaneous controls. All four models exhibit fading scalar memory and distinguish matched pulse-order histories in density, with no resolved general advantage for coupled CS. The distinction appears in the flow geometry: coupled evolution supports circulating and longitudinal history channels simultaneously, retains them briefly after input removal, and yields a combined-feature pulse-order accuracy of \(0.879\pm0.035\), compared with \(0.679\pm0.065\) for the instantaneous-transverse control. The evolved connection also cannot be reconstructed from an instantaneous density snapshot or replaced by a fitted local multiplier. We therefore find a task-specific advantage for geometry- and order-sensitive processing, rather than generic reservoir superiority. Here ``topological'' refers to the gauge organization of the state; the reported memory and cyclic-lag measures are not topological invariants.
tldr: The paper investigates whether a Chern-Simons context reservoir is a viable computational substrate and finds a task-specific advantage for geometry- and order-sensitive processing, but no generic reservoir superiority.
motivation: To determine if evolving a gauge connection in a Chern-Simons context reservoir provides computational benefits beyond simpler reservoir mechanisms.
method: Four matched models are compared—reciprocal transport, instantaneous transverse reconstruction, local nonlinear feedback, and fully coupled conserved-current Chern-Simons dynamics—across ten random seeds, testing stability, convergence, and memory.
result: Fully coupled CS dynamics preserves Gauss law and converges under refinement, but all models exhibit fading scalar memory; the coupled model achieves pulse-order accuracy of 0.879±0.035 versus 0.679±0.065 for the instantaneous-transverse control.
conclusion: The evolved connection cannot be reconstructed from an instantaneous density snapshot, yielding a task-specific advantage for geometry- and order-sensitive processing rather than generic reservoir superiority; the reported memory and cyclic-lag measures are not topological invariants.

title: A Catalogue Of Properties Of Binary Relations: Entailments, Incompatibilities, And Independence Results
authors: Magnus Boman
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13317v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study fifteen properties of binary relations that have established uses in modal logic, order and preference theory, and relation algebra. The organising question is pragmatic: once some properties of a relation are known, which further properties follow, which combinations force degeneracy, and which properties remain independent? We give a proved Horn basis of elementary and compound entailments, explicit countermodels for non-entailments, and a relation-algebraic translation of all fifteen properties. The modal discussion includes the usual Scott--Lemmon correspondences and the logic of transitive dense frames studied by Ghilardi and Mints. Exhaustive finite enumeration and targeted model search are used for discovery, while the catalogue is certified in Lean. A kernel-checked coverage calculation ranges over all 2^15 = 32,768 antecedent sets and all fifteen possible consequents. Its 51-rule Horn manifest is coupled definitionally to Lean proofs of semantic soundness, and its 49 witness rows are coupled definitionally to Lean-certified finite or infinite relations. Consequently, over non-empty domains, the Horn closure is complete for positive entailment among the fifteen selected properties, and the consistency classification is complete for their positive combinations.
tldr: A formally verified (Lean) catalogue of entailment, incompatibility, and independence relations among fifteen properties of binary relations used in modal logic, order theory, and relation algebra.
motivation: Researchers frequently need to know which combinations of relational properties are consistent, which imply others, and which are mutually independent, but this information was scattered across modal logic, preference theory, and relation algebra literature.
method: The authors compute a Horn basis of elementary and compound entailments via exhaustive finite enumeration and targeted model search, provide explicit countermodels for non-entailments, translate all fifteen properties into relation algebra, and certify the whole catalogue in Lean, including a kernel-checked coverage calculation over all 2^15 antecedent sets.
result: The paper yields a 51-rule Horn manifest and 49 witness rows machine-checked in Lean, establishing that over non-empty domains the Horn closure is complete for positive entailment among the fifteen properties and that the consistency classification is complete for their positive combinations.
conclusion: The result is a complete, formally verified reference catalogue for reasoning about entailment and compatibility among standard binary-relation properties, bridging classical logic, order theory, and mechanized proof.

title: BadEngram: Backdoor Attack On Gated Memory Components In LLMs
authors: Ariel Fogel, Omer Hofman, Eilon Cohen, Roman Vainshtein
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13478v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To expand open-weight models' capacity without proportionally increasing computation, recent language models incorporate gated parametric memories that retrieve learned values and inject them into intermediate representations. Despite these efficiency benefits, such modules create a distinct attack surface: their parameters can be modified independently of the backbone while directly shaping its computation. We introduce BadEngram, a post-training attack that exploits this surface to implant persistent, trigger-dependent behavior while leaving conventional backbone weights and the execution graph unchanged. We first establish the attack's feasibility and causally characterize its mechanism in a controlled Engram model, where BadEngram achieves 96.6% ASR on triggered inputs while limiting false activation on matched trigger-free inputs to 0.1% and preserving 99.6% clean accuracy. Replacing the retrieved memory values with their clean counterparts or closing the memory gates reduces ASR to at most 0.32%, confirming that the backdoor is expressed through the gated-memory pathway. We then test whether this vulnerability extends to production scale in Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's native Per-Layer Embedding subsystem. Using independently trained checkpoints for the two benchmarks, BadEngram achieves 50.4% ASR on HarmBench and 60.0% on AdvBench, while dormant-condition ASR remains 0.9% and 0.0%, respectively. These results identify native gated-memory parameters as a security-critical part of the model whose integrity cannot be inferred from an unchanged backbone.
tldr: BadEngram is a post-training backdoor attack that implants trigger-dependent behavior into the gated parametric memory modules of large language models while leaving backbone weights and the execution graph untouched.
motivation: Gated parametric memory modules (e.g., Engram-style memories and Qwen's Per-Layer Embedding subsystem) can be modified independently of the backbone, creating an overlooked attack surface for persistent backdoors.
method: The authors implant backdoors by editing only the gated-memory parameters, then causally verify the mechanism by substituting clean retrieved values or closing the memory gates, and scale the attack to Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's native Per-Layer Embedding subsystem.
result: The attack reaches 96.6% ASR with 0.1% false activation and 99.6% clean accuracy in a controlled Engram model, and 50.4% (HarmBench) / 60.0% (AdvBench) ASR at production scale with near-zero dormant-condition activation.
conclusion: Native gated-memory parameters constitute a security-critical component whose integrity cannot be inferred from an unchanged backbone, motivating new defenses and verification procedures.

title: Confuse The Model, Control The Flow: Understanding And Mitigating Privacy Leakage From Llm Agents With Information Flow Control
authors: Minsun Shim, Ramisha Raida Karim, Ruthwik Jakkula, Kaiwen Zhou, Xin Liu, Xin Eric Wang, Zhou Li
abstract: ArXiv:2609.14003v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Personal AI agents built on large language models (LLMs) are increasingly given access to a user's private data and communications in order to provide personalized assistance. This access creates a persistent privacy risk: the agent must decide whether a given sensitive information should be disclosed to a particular party. Existing defenses address this by making the agent's backend LLM more privacy-preserving through stronger system prompts, training, or explicit consent-checking procedures, but this approach has a structural challenge: whenever enforcement is a judgment the LLM makes over the same conversational context an adversary controls, the enforcement mechanism and the attack surface coincide. We demonstrate this against existing defenses with three new attacks that require only ordinary agent interaction and no prompt injection: Collaborative Workspace Lure reframes an extraction attempt as collaborative work; Semantic Obfuscation Attack induces disclosure through omission rather than through anything the agent writes; and Channel Decoupling Attack splits the extraction request and the disclosure across independent channels. All three achieve substantially higher leak rates than the attacks these defenses were originally designed to withstand. Guided by this observation, we present FLOWSEAL, a defense that enforces confidentiality through a tool-level interceptor outside the LLM's context, grounded in data provenance and an information-flow-control lattice with controlled declassification. Evaluated across three benchmarks, five prompt-based baselines, and eight attacks, including a real agent executing live tool calls through MCP, FLOWSEAL reduces leak rates to near zero (e.g., 52.2% to 0.5% against Collaborative Workspace Lure) while preserving task utility, regardless of the underlying LLM backend.
tldr: This paper exposes privacy leakage attacks on LLM-based personal agents and proposes FLOWSEAL, an information-flow-control tool-level interceptor that reduces leak rates to near zero while preserving utility.
motivation: LLM agents with access to users' private data must decide when to disclose sensitive information, but existing defenses rely on the same LLM's judgment over an adversary-controlled conversational context, creating a structural vulnerability where enforcement and attack surface coincide.
method: The authors introduce three new attacks (Collaborative Workspace Lure, Semantic Obfuscation Attack, and Channel Decoupling Attack) and build FLOWSEAL, which enforces confidentiality through a tool-level interceptor grounded in data provenance and an information-flow-control lattice with controlled declassification, operating outside the LLM's context.
result: Evaluated on three benchmarks, five prompt-based baselines, and eight attacks, including live tool calls via MCP, FLOWSEAL reduces leak rates to near zero (e.g., from 52.2% to 0.5% against Collaborative Workspace Lure) while maintaining task utility, regardless of the backend LLM.
conclusion: Enforcing privacy via information flow control outside the LLM's controllable context effectively mitigates agent privacy leakage, suggesting that confidentiality should be structurally enforced rather than left to the model's in-context judgment.

title: Neuron Activation-based Computation Of Logical Explanations For Deep Neural Networks
authors: Tom\'a\v{s} Kol\'arik, Faezeh Labbaf, Fabrizio Leopardi, Grigory Fedyukovich, Michael Wand, Natasha Sharygina
abstract: ArXiv:2609.14099v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Formal explainability of classifying neural networks (NNs) is an active area of research, providing explanations with provable guarantees of the classification within continuous regions of the input feature space. However, the existing techniques are either limited to individual input features without guarantees on their relations or the provided solutions fail to scale to deep architectures. This paper addresses these issues by introducing a flexible symbolic framework for an efficient, guided computation of explanations of the NN behavior, parametrized by the activations of internal neurons, and using logical engines such as SMT solvers. Unlike prior methods that rely on specialized NN verifiers, our method yields explanations that are not restricted in shape. Our algorithm is implementable on top of a general-purpose logical solver, isolating the NN-specific encoding from the algorithmic framework. We experimented with a wide range of benchmarks from the domains of image recognition and medicine, illustrating the advantages of the new method, particularly in computational efficiency. Notably, our approach enables logical explanation of deep networks not amenable to prior logic-based methods.
tldr: The paper introduces a symbolic framework that computes logical explanations for deep neural network classifications by parameterizing explanations on internal neuron activations and delegating reasoning to general-purpose SMT solvers.
motivation: Existing formal explainability methods either handle only individual input features without capturing relations between them, or fail to scale to deep architectures, limiting their practical usefulness.
method: The authors define a flexible symbolic encoding of the network's behavior guided by internal neuron activations, isolating the NN-specific encoding from the algorithmic framework so that any general-purpose logical engine (SMT solver) can compute explanations of unrestricted shape.
result: Experiments across image recognition and medical benchmarks show improved computational efficiency, and the approach succeeds on deep networks that prior logic-based explanation methods could not handle.
conclusion: Decoupling NN encoding from a general logical solver enables scalable, provably guaranteed logical explanations for deep networks, broadening the scope of formal explainability.

title: Dynamically-scaled Local Patch Method For Numerically Simulating The Scattering Effects Of Small Particles Into Large Beams
authors: Ryan Derosa Kohei Yamamoto
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13528v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Simulating the propagation of a large beam with high spatial resolution is a common challenge in optics due to both computational time and memory demands. While computational time sets a practical limit on what one can simulate, memory resources are an absolute hard limit. In this paper, we report a novel method to overcome a gap in spatial scale between the beam and the relatively small optical disturbance that needs to be modeled, such as those due to particulate contamination. The method splits the entire propagation chain into to two paths: a specular field propagation on coarse grids and scattered fields on fine grids. Especially for the latter, we dynamically apply high-resolution local patches for individual particles. Not limited to particulate contamination, this method is applicable to any tiny discontinuous structures on the beam propagation path without memory overflow triggered.
tldr: The paper introduces a dynamically-scaled local patch numerical method that splits beam propagation into coarse-grid specular fields and fine-grid scattered fields to simulate scattering from small particles in large beams without memory overflow.
motivation: Simulating large-beam propagation at high spatial resolution is limited by computational memory, especially when small optical disturbances such as particulate contamination must be resolved.
method: The propagation chain is split into two paths: specular field propagation on coarse grids and scattered field propagation on fine grids, with high-resolution local patches dynamically applied around individual particles.
result: The approach avoids memory overflow and enables spatially resolved simulation of small discontinuous structures on the beam path that would otherwise be infeasible with uniform fine grids.
conclusion: The method is generalizable to any tiny discontinuous structure along a beam propagation path, not only particulate contamination, providing a practical numerical tool for classical optics simulation.

title: Characterizing Resonant Solitary States As Relative Equilibria Via Normal Form Reduction
authors: Bob Rink Bengi D\"onmez
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate solitary states in coupled oscillator networks, where a single oscillator detaches from a synchronized cluster and evolves at a distinct mean frequency. We focus on resonant solitary states, in which the mean frequency of the detached oscillator is shaped by resonance with a mode of the cluster. Here, we introduce a normal-form and symmetry-based approach to identify such states. We reduce the high-dimensional network dynamics to a two-dimensional second-order system that couples a rotator representing the solitary oscillator to a harmonic oscillator representing the dominant Laplacian mode of the cluster. We use normal-form transformations to introduce symmetry into this system. Using this symmetry, we reformulate the frequency selection problem as the search for relative equilibria of the normal form symmetry. We derive explicit algebraic conditions for the existence of these relative equilibria, and hence for resonant solitary states and their effective frequencies.
tldr: The paper introduces a normal-form and symmetry-based reduction to characterize resonant solitary states in coupled oscillator networks as relative equilibria of a two-dimensional rotator-oscillator system.
motivation: Resonant solitary states, where a detached oscillator's mean frequency locks to a cluster mode, lack a systematic analytical framework for predicting their existence and effective frequencies.
method: The high-dimensional network dynamics are reduced to a two-dimensional second-order system coupling a rotator (solitary oscillator) and a harmonic oscillator (dominant Laplacian mode), then normal-form transformations are applied to introduce a symmetry that recasts frequency selection as a search for relative equilibria.
result: Explicit algebraic conditions are derived for the existence of these relative equilibria, yielding conditions for resonant solitary states and their effective frequencies.
conclusion: The symmetry-based normal-form reduction provides an analytical handle on resonant solitary states and their frequency selection in oscillator networks.

title: $\varepsilon$-isometries Without Isometric Embeddings
authors: Yipeng Zhang Longfa Sun
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that there exist two separable real Banach spaces [MATH] and [MATH] such that, for every [MATH], there is a standard exact [MATH]-isometry [MATH] whose distortion of every distance is between [MATH] and [MATH], whereas no isometric embedding of [MATH] into [MATH] exists, even without a linearity assumption. This gives a negative answer to \cite[Problem 1 and Problem 2]{cheng4} of Cheng and Zhou. The construction combines a snowflaked Lipschitz-free space with the Schur-property theorem of Kalton and the isometric linearization theorem of Godefroy and Kalton.
tldr: The paper constructs two separable real Banach spaces that admit approximate (ε-)isometries at every scale but no isometric embedding, resolving two open problems of Cheng and Zhou.
motivation: Cheng and Zhou asked whether the existence of standard exact ε-isometries at arbitrarily small distortion implies the existence of an isometric embedding, and the authors aim to settle both problems negatively.
method: The construction combines a snowflaked Lipschitz-free space with Kalton's Schur-property theorem and the Godefroy–Kalton isometric linearization theorem.
result: Two separable real Banach spaces are exhibited such that for every ε there is a standard exact ε-isometry whose distortion lies between 1 and 1+ε, yet no isometric embedding between them exists even without linearity.
conclusion: The results give a negative answer to Cheng and Zhou's Problems 1 and 2 and clarify the gap between approximate and exact nonlinear isometric structure in Banach space theory.

title: Opacity Predictions In Plasmas Under Stellar Conditions Using Deep Learning
authors: Jean-Christophe Pain Djamel Benredjem
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13252v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The aim of this work is to predict the opacity of plasmas under stellar conditions. We focus on iron and nickel, as these elements have been extensively investigated both theoretically and experimentally. In certain regimes, notably under non-local thermodynamic equilibrium, calculating the spectral opacity can be computationally demanding. To mitigate this difficulty, we employ deep learning models to predict accurate opacities while achieving a substantial reduction in computational cost. Specifically, we develop and train a hybrid model that combines a convolutional neural network with a multilayer perceptron. The proposed approach provides both the spectral opacity over the 0--10,000 eV energy range, and the corresponding mean opacities for large sets of temperatures and mass densities, in close agreement with standard computational methods. The agreement is very satisfactory, except in the L- and M-shell energy ranges for nickel at high temperatures, where a very large number of emerging transitions leads to substantial discrepancies.
tldr: This paper trains a hybrid CNN-MLP deep learning model to predict spectral and mean opacities of iron and nickel plasmas under stellar conditions, achieving large computational speedups over standard atomic-physics calculations.
motivation: Spectral opacity calculations for plasmas in non-local thermodynamic equilibrium are computationally expensive, motivating a surrogate modeling approach that preserves accuracy at much lower cost.
method: The authors develop and train a hybrid convolutional neural network plus multilayer perceptron architecture to regress spectral opacity over the 0-10,000 eV range and mean opacities across large grids of temperature and mass density.
result: Predictions agree closely with standard computational opacity codes across most regimes, with notable discrepancies in the L- and M-shell energy ranges for nickel at high temperatures due to the very large number of emerging transitions.
conclusion: Deep learning offers a viable, much cheaper alternative for opacity prediction in stellar plasma modeling, though accuracy in transition-dense regimes remains a limitation.

title: Momentum Microscopy Of Ultrafast Electron Emission From A Strongly Driven Optical Nanoantenna
authors: Kerstin Harland, Germann Hergert, Zsuzsanna P\'apa, Xiaofei Wu, Lina Hansen, Julia Altenburg, Katrin Meier, Arvid Kl\"osgen, Bert Hecht, Jer-Shing Huang, P\'eter Dombi, Jan Vogelsang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13354v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Metallic nanostructures in combination with femtosecond lasers are a well-suited platform for the control of photoelectrons by strong and nano-localized driving fields, with high relevance for ultrafast, coherent electron emitters and petahertz electronics. Photoelectron spectroscopy resolves such photoelectron dynamics, but lacks nanoscale spatial resolution, making it only suited for single emitters or homogeneous arrays. We report the first strong-field experiment combining both photoemission electron microscopy and momentum microscopy, two complementary techniques providing spatial and momentum resolution within the same instrument. We apply this new methodology to a double-hole nanoantenna with sub-10 nm apex radii, demonstrating the potential of this approach for the control of photoelectrons in heterogeneous nanostructured samples using few-cycle light fields. Our measurements reveal distinct signatures of two classes of electron trajectories in the near-field. Quiver trajectories result in directed, angularly more focused emission, whereas subcycle trajectories give rise to a broader transverse momentum distribution. Surprisingly, this observation disagrees with previously reported emission characteristics from nanotip emitters, which we classify as a special case of a broader class of curved emitter surfaces driven by ultrashort light fields. This demonstrates both the impact of sophisticated electron detection methods and the potential of strong-field control of electrons in nanoscale geometries.
tldr: The paper combines photoemission electron microscopy and momentum microscopy to resolve ultrafast strong-field electron emission from a double-hole optical nanoantenna.
motivation: Metallic nanostructures driven by femtosecond lasers enable nanoscale control of photoelectrons, but existing photoelectron spectroscopy lacks spatial resolution and cannot easily study heterogeneous nanostructured samples.
method: The authors perform a strong-field experiment using a single instrument that provides both spatial and momentum resolution, applying it to a double-hole nanoantenna with sub-10 nm apex radii under few-cycle light fields.
result: They observe two classes of near-field electron trajectories: quiver trajectories giving directed, angularly focused emission, and subcycle trajectories producing a broader transverse momentum distribution, differing from previously reported nanotip emission characteristics.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a powerful methodology for controlling photoelectrons in heterogeneous nanoscale geometries and classifies nanotip emitters as a special case of curved emitter surfaces driven by ultrashort light fields.

title: Refractive Index Dispersion Fingerprinting Via Scanning-Free Parallel Multi-Wavelength Spr On A Single Aluminum Film
authors: Zihao Luo, Zhiying Chen, Yueqian Zhang, Xue Liu, Changsen Sun, Dmitry Kiesewetter, Sergey Krivosheev, Sergey Magazinov, Victor Malyugin, Xue Han
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Real-time characterization of refractive index (RI) dispersion is pivotal for advanced optical sensing, yet conventional surface plasmon resonance (SPR) platforms are bottlenecked by the narrow bandwidth of noble metals (Au, Ag) and the mechanical instability of sequential scanning. Here, we report a novel Al-based parallel SPR platform that overcomes the bandwidth and temporal constraints of conventional noble-metal systems. Leveraging the unique low-loss broadband response of Al, enabled by the suppression of interband transitions, we engineered a system for simultaneous excitation at 450, 520, and 635 nm. By integrating spectral-angle multiplexing with RGB-channel demultiplexing on a CMOS camera, the platform achieved acquisition of dispersion profiles without mechanical motion. Validated against NaCl solutions, the system demonstrates metrological accuracy and exceptional agreement with Cauchy dispersion models. The proposed architecture eliminates temporal drift and vibration errors, establishing a new benchmark for real-time dispersion characterization. By decoupling sensing from mechanical constraints, this work pioneers a compact, robust framework for next-generation, field-deployable sensors capable of distinguishing complex analytes via their unique spectral signatures.
tldr: An aluminum-based parallel multi-wavelength surface plasmon resonance platform enables scanning-free, real-time refractive index dispersion characterization of analytes.
motivation: Conventional SPR sensors using noble metals (Au, Ag) are limited by narrow bandwidth and mechanical scanning instabilities, hampering real-time dispersion measurement.
method: The authors exploit aluminum's low-loss broadband plasmonic response to simultaneously excite SPR at 450, 520, and 635 nm, using spectral-angle multiplexing with RGB-channel demultiplexing on a CMOS camera for motion-free acquisition.
result: The platform produced dispersion profiles for NaCl solutions that agreed well with Cauchy dispersion models, achieving metrological accuracy without temporal drift or vibration artifacts.
conclusion: The work establishes a compact, robust, field-deployable refractive-index dispersion sensing architecture, though it lies outside quantum information science.

title: Exceptional-point Conjugate Symmetry And Migration In Fluid-loaded Elastic Waveguides: Restructuring The Physical Dispersion Spectrum
authors: Dong Xiao, Zahra Sharif Khodaei, M. H. Aliabadi
abstract: ArXiv:2609.14061v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The dispersion spectrum of a fluid-loaded elastic waveguide is a non-Hermitian system with eigenmodes on a two-sheeted Riemann manifold. Although exceptional points (EPs) organize avoided crossings, the topological rules by which fluid loading restructures the observable spectrum (both physically admissible modes and their connectivity) remain unknown, and conventional solvers fail to recover complete branches. Here we establish these rules. We prove that, for real elastic moduli and real fluid parameters, EPs obey a conjugate-pair symmetry, and that a pair on the physical sheet enforces an avoided crossing of real wavenumbers between the two modes it controls, yielding a topological criterion for mode identification. We then identify two independent reconstruction mechanisms. First, the physical observation space expands continuously: a mode observable above its vacuum cut-off can extend downward to the sound line, admitting solutions in a frequency band empty in vacuum; vacuum-anchored seeds above cut-offs continued downward capture such branches systematically. Second, EP migration rewires mode connectivity: as fluid density increases, conjugate pairs leaving the physical sheet (signaled by a sign reversal of the imaginary part of either the in-plane or the vertical wavenumber) leave the two previously coupled physical branch segments unconnected by any EP within the observation space; they become independent curves that may intersect freely on the real frequency axis, with the narrowest veerings losing their topological protection first. Mirror-symmetry breaking births additional EPs generically in the trapped regime but only conditionally in the leaky regime. Numerical computations on symmetric and asymmetric composite laminates under single- and double-sided water loading validate the framework, recovering multiple leaky branches missed by standard solvers.
tldr: This paper derives topological rules for exceptional points and mode connectivity in fluid-loaded elastic waveguides, a classical non-Hermitian acoustics problem unrelated to quantum information.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how fluid loading restructures the physical dispersion spectrum of elastic waveguides and to recover leaky branches missed by standard solvers.
method: They prove a conjugate-pair symmetry for exceptional points, identify two spectral reconstruction mechanisms, and validate the framework with numerical computations on symmetric and asymmetric composite laminates under water loading.
result: Exceptional points obey conjugate-pair symmetry, and their migration rewires mode connectivity, expanding the observable frequency bands and producing additional exceptional points in trapped and leaky regimes.
conclusion: The framework provides a topological criterion for mode identification and successfully recovers multiple leaky branches previously missed by conventional solvers.

title: A New Six Parameters Generalized Weibull-Kumaraswamy-{Lomax) Distribution With A Novel Linear Series Expansion Of Its Probability Density
authors: Iman Mohamed Attia
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13316v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: One method of generalizing a distribution is to add new parameter to the baseline distribution. In this paper the author discusses this methodology to create a new six parameters generalized Weibull-Kumaraswamy-{Lomax) Distribution. The author utilizes the approach of the T-X{Y} family to add new parameters the baseline distribution Kumaraswamy distribution defined on the unit interval with two shape parameters a & b>0. The author used the Lomax distribution with two parameters {\alpha} & {\lambda}>0 , scale and shape parameters respectively, to link the baseline distribution with the generator distribution. The generator distribution is the Weibull distribution with the two parameters, c & {\gamma}>0 , shape and scale parameters respectively as will be explained in the paper. The result is a new distribution with six parameters. The author derived the PDF, CDF, and quantile functions. The author used a new technique to expand the pdf in a linear series expansion that is simple and does not require special function. This makes the computational statistics for the raw moments easier and simpler. The author discusses the Shannon entropy and the paper contains figures for the PDF, CDF and the quantile functions.
tldr: The paper introduces a new six-parameter generalized Weibull-Kumaraswamy-Lomax distribution along with a novel linear series expansion of its probability density function.
motivation: Generalizing baseline distributions by adding parameters increases flexibility in modeling real data, and existing expansions of the density function often require special functions that complicate moment computations.
method: The author combines the T-X{Y} family approach with a Kumaraswamy baseline, a Lomax linker, and a Weibull generator, then derives the PDF, CDF, and quantile functions and develops a new linear series expansion of the PDF that avoids special functions.
result: A closed-form six-parameter distribution is obtained whose density admits a simple linear series expansion, simplifying raw moment and Shannon entropy computations, with accompanying figures for PDF, CDF, and quantile functions.
conclusion: The proposed distribution offers a computationally convenient, highly flexible statistical model, though the work is purely in classical distribution theory with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Formation Control From The Generic Combinatorial Viewpoint: Edge Dynamics And Directed Sensing
authors: Louis Theran, Daniel Zelazo, Sean Dewar, Bernd Schulze
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13423v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a geometric framework for distance-based formation control that separates the evolution of inter-agent distances from its realization by compatible node motions, reducing the stability problem to the edge space. We show that local exponential convergence of the edge dynamics implies local exponential convergence of the formation, and that stability is certified by spectral properties of a linear edge operator. We introduce a hierarchy of generic spectral properties --- weak admissibility, admissibility, and strong admissibility --- that provide necessary conditions for local exponential stability. Specializing to directed sensing, we obtain a necessary and sufficient spectral condition for local stability at an arbitrary target, together with a quadratic sufficient certificate. These conditions reveal that stability depends jointly on the graph orientation and target geometry, and show that persistence is neither necessary nor sufficient for local convergence. We show that every generically rigid graph admits an admissible orientation and, for acyclic orientations, we give an exact combinatorial characterization of admissibility. Finally, the quadratic certificate leads to a semidefinite program for synthesizing stabilizing edge gains.
tldr: The paper develops a geometric and combinatorial framework for distance-based formation control, reducing stability to edge dynamics and spectral properties of directed sensing graphs.
motivation: Distance-based formation control typically relies on persistence or rigidity conditions, which are not sufficient nor necessary for convergence; the authors seek a more fundamental spectral characterization.
method: They separate inter-agent distance evolution from compatible node motions, introduce generic spectral properties (weak admissibility, admissibility, strong admissibility), and derive necessary and sufficient conditions for directed sensing via a quadratic sufficient certificate.
result: Local exponential convergence of edge dynamics implies formation convergence, stability depends jointly on graph orientation and target geometry, persistence is neither necessary nor sufficient, and every generically rigid graph admits an admissible orientation.
conclusion: The framework yields a semidefinite program for synthesizing stabilizing edge gains and provides a combinatorial characterization of admissibility for acyclic orientations.

title: Inverse Learning Of The Altruism And Cost Level In Mixed-Individual Mean Field Games
authors: Haoyang Cao, G\"ok\c{c}e Dayan{\i}kl{\i}, Xiaofei Shi
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13469v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding how humans respond to incentives, both at the individual and collective levels, is crucial to the design of effective policies. Within the continuous-time stochastic framework for large interacting populations, mean field games (MFGs) model populations of non-cooperative agents, whereas mean field control (MFC) describes the fully cooperative benchmark, interpreted in our setting as fully altruistic behavior. Mixed-individual MFGs interpolate between these two extremes through a parameter governing the degree of altruism. A central challenge for regulators and policymakers, however, is that intrinsic altruism levels and other private structural parameters, such as individual labor costs, are typically unobservable. To address this challenge, we develop an inverse learning framework for mixed-individual MFGs. Our approach enables the recovery of (latent) altruism and labor cost levels from noisy observations, with experiments demonstrating the feasibility and accuracy of our method. These findings underscore the promise of inverse MFG methodologies for uncovering latent preference structures in large populations, with important implications for incentive design, empirical behavioral modeling, and data-driven policy analysis.
tldr: The paper develops an inverse learning framework for mixed-individual mean field games to recover latent altruism and labor cost parameters from noisy observations.
motivation: Regulators and policymakers need to infer private preference parameters such as altruism and individual costs in large populations, but these quantities are typically unobservable.
method: The authors formulate an inverse learning problem within continuous-time mixed-individual mean field games, interpolating between non-cooperative MFGs and fully cooperative mean field control, and use noisy observations to estimate structural parameters.
result: Experiments demonstrate that the proposed method can recover latent altruism and labor cost levels with feasible accuracy from noisy data.
conclusion: Inverse MFG methodologies show promise for uncovering latent preference structures in large populations, with implications for incentive design and data-driven policy analysis.

title: Generative Bootstrap Processes
authors: Fang Han Ziming Lin
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13471v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study generative bootstrap processes obtained by resampling from fitted generative distributions. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for their conditional weak convergence to the [MATH]-Brownian bridge, formulated in terms of finite-dimensional conditional weak convergence and conditional asymptotic equicontinuity. We further provide general sufficient conditions and a Gin\'e-Zinn-type characterization relating this convergence to the [MATH]-Donsker property. As applications, we verify these conditions for prominent classes of generative models, including triangular normalizing flows, flow matching, score-based diffusion models, and Wasserstein generative adversarial networks.
tldr: The paper develops generative bootstrap processes and establishes conditional weak convergence conditions to the Brownian bridge for resampling from fitted generative models.
motivation: Bootstrap methods are widely used for uncertainty quantification, but their theoretical behavior under modern generative models is not well understood.
method: The authors derive necessary and sufficient conditions for conditional weak convergence in terms of finite-dimensional conditional weak convergence and conditional asymptotic equicontinuity, and provide a Giné-Zinn-type characterization linked to the Donsker property.
result: They verify the conditions for triangular normalizing flows, flow matching, score-based diffusion models, and Wasserstein GANs.
conclusion: The work provides a general theoretical framework for generative bootstrap processes and demonstrates its applicability across several prominent generative model classes.

title: From Priors To Projections: Geometry And Simplified Mimo Demodulation Of Probabilistic Shaping
authors: Kirill Ivanov, Wei Yang, Mahmoud Taherzadeh Boroujeni, Jing Jiang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13492v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Probabilistic shaping (PS) is a well-known method to achieve improved performance upon a regular quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) by taking the target constellation and making the distribution of underlying points non-uniform. It has been extensively studied over the years for the additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) and Rayleigh fading channels. However, the potential of probabilistic shaping in the multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) setting needs further investigations. In this paper, we prove that if shaped symbols follow Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution, the optimal maximum a posteriori (MAP) detection is equivalent to the case of uniform constellation with a simple preprocessing step. Our approach has multiple benefits. It enables to utilize the same processing chain for both shaped and unshaped system, which simplifies the receiver architecture. This technique can be applied for both linear MMSE and nonlinear (near-)MAP demapper types. In addition, the complexity of adaptive methods such as sphere decoding can be reduced.
tldr: The paper proves that for Maxwell-Boltzmann probabilistically shaped constellations, optimal MAP detection in MIMO systems reduces to the uniform-constellation case with a simple preprocessing step, simplifying receiver design and reducing demapper complexity.
motivation: Probabilistic shaping is well studied for AWGN and Rayleigh fading channels but its potential in the MIMO setting remains under-investigated, and existing receivers for shaped systems are complex and architecturally distinct from unshaped ones.
method: The authors derive an analytical equivalence showing that MAP detection with Maxwell-Boltzmann-distributed shaped symbols maps onto a uniform-constellation detection problem via a preprocessing (projection/geometry) transformation, applicable to both linear MMSE and nonlinear near-MAP demappers as well as sphere decoding.
result: The transformation lets the same processing chain serve both shaped and unshaped systems, simplifies receiver architecture, reduces complexity of adaptive methods like sphere decoding, and unifies demapper treatment across linear and nonlinear types.
conclusion: Probabilistic shaping in MIMO can be handled with a simplified, unified demodulation framework, lowering implementation complexity without sacrificing the shaping gains.

title: Nonsmooth Optimization Via Orthogonalized Momentum
authors: Lexiao Lai, Tianyi Lin, Jiayu Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13677v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern real application problems involve matrix-valued parameters, yet conventional optimizers treat them as vectors, thereby motivating matrix-aware methods that exploit input-output geometry, such as Muon which orthogonalizes the momentum matrices before parameter updates. Its empirical success raises a conceptual question: can orthogonalized momentum remain effective beyond smooth optimization? This paper studies this question for locally Lipschitz functions using a generalized derivative framework compatible with backpropagation. Our first contribution is to identify a key limitation: for every fixed momentum factor [MATH], Muon can fail to approach the global optimal solution of a convex Lipschitz objective from almost every initialization, when step sizes adapt to the full gradient history. The failure can occur even along bounded iterates. Our example is inspired by the one of Parshakova et al. which only covers [MATH]. Then, we show that the obstruction lies in fixed momentum rather than orthogonalization. Indeed, when the momentum factor is adaptive and approaches 1 together with a vanishing step size, Muon recovers asymptotic convergence for nonconvex nonsmooth optimization under the boundedness and regularity conditions. Moreover, we propose MAGD, which combines orthogonalized momentum with gradient, weighted based on their relative progress. MAGD retains asymptotic convergence in nonconvex settings and achieves an [MATH] rate in convex settings. A lower bound shows the optimal dimension dependence. Experiments on synthetic problems, image classification, and LLM pretraining show MAGD is a simple and practical alternative to Muon. Together, our results characterize when orthogonalized momentum fails without smoothness and how it can be made reliable and we hope that the analysis may be useful more broadly.
tldr: The paper analyzes when orthogonalized-momentum optimizers like Muon fail for nonsmooth locally Lipschitz objectives and proposes MAGD, an adaptive momentum variant with convergence guarantees and empirical gains.
motivation: Matrix-valued parameters are common in modern applications, and matrix-aware methods such as Muon (which orthogonalizes momentum before updates) have shown empirical success, but it is unclear whether orthogonalized momentum remains effective outside smooth optimization.
method: Using a generalized derivative framework compatible with backpropagation, the authors construct a failure example for fixed-momentum Muon on convex Lipschitz objectives, then propose MAGD, which combines orthogonalized momentum with gradient weighted by relative progress and adaptive momentum approaching 1 with vanishing step size.
result: Fixed momentum provably prevents convergence from almost every initialization even along bounded iterates, whereas adaptive momentum restores asymptotic convergence for nonconvex nonsmooth problems; MAGD achieves an optimal-rate result in convex settings matching a lower bound on dimension dependence, with experiments on synthetic tasks, image classification, and LLM pretraining.
conclusion: The obstruction to Muon in nonsmooth settings lies in fixed momentum rather than orthogonalization itself, and making momentum adaptive yields a simple, reliable, practical alternative to Muon.

title: Relative Mean Sensitivity And Relative Entropy Under Group Actions
authors: Wenqi Ouyang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13817v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we introduce relative mean sensitivity both in topological and measure-theoretical settings under group actions. It turns out that relative positive entropy is relative mean [MATH]-sensitive between minimal systems; relative positive [MATH]-entropy for an ergodic measure [MATH] is relative mean [MATH]-[MATH]-sensitive.
tldr: The paper introduces relative mean sensitivity in topological and measure-theoretic settings for group actions and links it to relative positive entropy.
motivation: Sensitivity and entropy are classical indicators of chaotic behavior in dynamical systems; the authors aim to extend these notions to a relative (fiber-wise) framework for group actions.
method: They define relative mean sensitivity and relative mean N-sensitivity, then prove implications from relative positive entropy (topological and measure-theoretic) to these sensitivity notions between minimal systems.
result: Relative positive entropy between minimal systems implies relative mean sensitivity, and relative positive N-entropy for an ergodic measure implies relative mean N-sensitivity.
conclusion: The findings extend classical entropy–sensitivity bridges to the relative setting, contributing to abstract topological and ergodic dynamics theory.

title: An Integral Representation Of Eigenfunctions For The Deformed Noumi--Sano Operators
authors: Takahiko Nobukawa Taikei Fujii
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13837v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The deformed Noumi-Sano operator [MATH] of order [MATH] is a simultaneous extension of the Macdonald operator and the Noumi-Sano operator. In this paper, we construct an integral transform associated with eigenvalue problem of [MATH]. Using the integral transform, we obtain an integral representation of eigenfunctions for [MATH].
tldr: The paper constructs an integral transform for the deformed Noumi-Sano operator and uses it to obtain an integral representation of its eigenfunctions.
motivation: The deformed Noumi-Sano operator simultaneously generalizes the Macdonald operator and the Noumi-Sano operator, and its spectral theory is of interest in special functions and integrable systems.
method: The authors introduce an integral transform adapted to the eigenvalue problem of the deformed Noumi-Sano operator and derive eigenfunctions through this transform.
result: An integral representation of the eigenfunctions for the deformed Noumi-Sano operator is established.
conclusion: The work provides a new analytic tool for studying generalized Noumi-Sano operators and their eigenfunctions, with potential applications in mathematical physics.

title: Can One Regularizer Reproduce Posterior Means At Two Noise Levels?
authors: Kang Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consider Gaussian denoising with a fixed prior and varying noise variance. When the prior has a density, maximum a posteriori estimation uses its negative logarithm as a fixed regularizer; only the weight of the quadratic data term changes with the noise variance. We ask whether a fixed regularizer can also recover the posterior mean. Although a suitable regularizer exists at each variance, we prove that no single regularizer works at two distinct positive variances for any compactly supported prior other than a point mass. This holds even for nonconvex and nonsmooth regularizers. A residual computed from two denoiser evaluations gives positive lower bounds on the uniform approximation error and excess mean squared error of estimators using a common regularizer. Numerical examples illustrate these bounds and the cost of reusing a regularizer across noise levels.
tldr: The paper proves that no single regularizer can recover the posterior mean at two distinct Gaussian noise variances for any non-degenerate compactly supported prior, even allowing nonconvex and nonsmooth regularizers.
motivation: Maximum a posteriori estimation corresponds to using the prior's negative log-density as a fixed regularizer while only the data-term weight varies with noise. The authors ask whether the same fixed regularizer can also yield the posterior mean.
method: They analyze Gaussian denoising with a fixed prior and varying noise variance, proving impossibility under compactly supported priors and deriving lower bounds on uniform approximation error and excess mean squared error from two denoiser evaluations.
result: No single regularizer works at two distinct positive variances except for a point-mass prior, and the residual from two denoiser evaluations provides positive lower bounds on approximation and MSE excess when reusing a regularizer.
conclusion: Reusing a regularizer across noise levels is fundamentally limited, with numerical examples illustrating the bounds and the cost of regularizer reuse.

title: Subspace Embeddings With The Rerandomized Srht
authors: Yuning Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13946v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work studies subspace embeddings obtained by two normalized real Walsh transforms, two independent sign diagonals, and uniform coordinate sampling without replacement. The main result shows that the prescribed sample size [MATH], for a universal constant [MATH], suffices to preserve all squared norms on each fixed [MATH]-dimensional subspace within [MATH] with probability at least [MATH]. The result holds for every ambient Walsh dimension and all ranks, and answers Problem TR-01 in the Open Problems in Numerical Linear Algebra repository. The proof controls joint entry cumulants of the transformed projection through connected graph contractions and Walsh character identities. These estimates then bound the expected trace of even powers of a product of centered projections. A two-projection decomposition converts this estimate into control of both spectral edges. Bernoulli sampling at arbitrary densities and a deterministic upper bound near full sampling yield the prescribed number of coordinates.
tldr: This paper proves that a subsampled randomized Walsh-Hadamard transform with two sign diagonals and uniform sampling without replacement yields subspace embeddings with a prescribed sample size.
motivation: Subspace embeddings are fundamental in randomized numerical linear algebra for dimensionality reduction, and the paper aims to resolve an open problem on the sample complexity of the rerandomized SRHT.
method: The proof controls joint entry cumulants of the transformed projection via connected graph contractions and Walsh character identities, then bounds the expected trace of even powers of a product of centered projections and uses a two-projection decomposition for spectral edge control.
result: The main theorem shows that M = O(d log d) samples suffice to preserve all squared norms on any fixed d-dimensional subspace up to 1±ε with high probability, for every ambient Walsh dimension and all ranks.
conclusion: The work answers Problem TR-01 in the Open Problems in Numerical Linear Algebra repository and advances the theory of subspace embeddings, but it is purely classical numerical linear algebra with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Prism-ude: Physics-Regularized Iterative Symbolic Modeling Of 3nm FinFETs Via Universal Differential Equation
authors: Pranavanath Balamurali, Prathamesh Dinesh Joshi, Raj Abhijit Dandekar, Rajat Dandekar, Sreedath Panat
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13200v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Compact transistor models are the mathematical backbone of circuit simulation. However, at advanced nodes such as 3nm, transport physics becomes too complex for traditional hand-derived equations to capture accurately. Purely data-driven neural surrogates, on the other hand, are numerically unstable inside circuit solvers and offer no physical insight into their own predictions. We introduce PRISM-UDE (Physics-Regularized Iterative Symbolic Modeling via Universal Differential Equations), a framework that embeds a small neural network inside a physics-based transistor model, using the network only to learn the transport behavior that the analytical baseline misses, rather than replacing the physics altogether. Once trained, this neural correction is distilled into a single, interpretable closed-form expression via symbolic regression, making the final model fully analytical and simulator-ready. Applied to a 3nm FinFET benchmark dataset, PRISM-UDE reduces prediction error more than sixfold (70.33% to 11.01%) relative to the standard physics-only baseline. The distilled expression preserves this accuracy almost exactly while eliminating the neural network entirely. We further validate the extracted expression directly inside a SPICE circuit simulator, confirming stable, physically consistent behavior under both static bias sweeps and dynamic switching conditions.
tldr: PRISM-UDE combines a physics-based compact model with a neural correction that is distilled into a closed-form expression for accurate and simulator-ready 3nm FinFET modeling.
motivation: Traditional hand-derived compact transistor models cannot capture complex 3nm transport physics, while purely data-driven neural surrogates are numerically unstable in circuit simulators and offer no physical insight.
method: The framework embeds a small neural network inside a physics-based transistor model to learn only the missing transport behavior, then uses symbolic regression to distill the neural correction into an interpretable closed-form expression.
result: On a 3nm FinFET benchmark, PRISM-UDE reduces prediction error from 70.33% to 11.01%, and the distilled analytical expression preserves this accuracy while eliminating the neural network; SPICE validation confirms stable static and dynamic behavior.
conclusion: Physics-regularized symbolic modeling can produce accurate, interpretable, and simulator-ready compact models for advanced semiconductor nodes.

title: E-als: Approximation-Potential-Aware E-Graph Rewriting For Approximate Logic Synthesis
authors: Bin Sun, Jianan Mu, Jiaxi Zhang, Rengang Zhang, Zhiteng Chao, Jing Ye, Huawei Li
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13276v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Approximate logic synthesis (ALS) improves circuit power, performance, and area by trading exact correctness for bounded functional error. However, existing structural ALS methods largely overlook structural bias: even functionally equivalent netlists can expose markedly different approximation opportunities and lead to substantially different outcomes under the same downstream ALS flow. Our experiments show that this effect can induce final area gaps of up to 42.77%. To unlock this opportunity, we propose E-ALS, an e-graph-based framework for approximation-aware structural search. E-ALS combines Function-Reduced Saturation, an ALS-coupled surrogate, search-based extraction, and budget-guided refinement to identify approximation-friendly equivalent structures. Experiments on well-established arithmetic and logic benchmarks show that E-ALS achieves additional area reductions of 3.2 and 7.0 percentage points under maximum Hamming-Distance and Error-Distance constraints, respectively. Code is available in [URL].
tldr: E-ALS is an e-graph-based framework for approximation-aware structural search in approximate logic synthesis, exploiting structural bias to find netlists more amenable to approximation.
motivation: Existing structural ALS methods overlook structural bias: functionally equivalent netlists can offer very different approximation opportunities, causing final area gaps of up to 42.77% under the same downstream flow.
method: The framework combines Function-Reduced Saturation, an ALS-coupled surrogate model, search-based extraction, and budget-guided refinement to identify approximation-friendly equivalent structures within an e-graph.
result: On standard arithmetic and logic benchmarks, E-ALS achieves additional area reductions of 3.2 and 7.0 percentage points under maximum Hamming-Distance and Error-Distance constraints, respectively.
conclusion: Approximation-aware structural search via e-graph rewriting yields tangible area improvements in approximate logic synthesis, though the work is purely classical EDA and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Scaling Chance-Constrained Correlated Equilibrium Computation For Exclusive Resource-Assignment Games
authors: Jaehan Im, Ufuk Topcu, David Fridovich-Keil
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13565v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The chance-constrained correlated equilibrium concept provides a robust coordination technique for self-interested agents whose costs are uncertain to a central coordinator, but the number of joint actions considered in its computation grows exponentially with the number of agents. We propose an exact-one resource-assignment restriction for games in which agents compete for shared resources and simultaneous use of a resource is undesirable or unsafe. The restriction allows each resource to be assigned to exactly one agent, reducing the number of joint actions considered from O(2^(nr)) to O(n^r) for n agents and r resources. The resulting problem is solved over the restricted joint action set while retaining all incentive constraints associated with unilateral deviations. We show that the feasible set of the restricted problem is exactly the convex hull of the chance-constrained pure Nash equilibria contained in the exact-one assignment set, yielding a necessary and sufficient condition for nonemptiness. We further derive a sufficient condition under which all chance-constrained pure Nash equilibria of the unrestricted game are retained by the restriction. Numerical experiments in a vertiport departure-corridor coordination scenario demonstrate a 99.81% reduction in median computation time relative to the unrestricted formulation while achieving equivalent coordination performance.
tldr: The paper proposes an exact-one resource-assignment restriction that makes chance-constrained correlated equilibrium computation tractable for multi-agent resource-allocation games.
motivation: Chance-constrained correlated equilibrium offers robust coordination under uncertain costs, but its computation scales exponentially in the number of agents because of the joint action space.
method: The authors impose an exact-one assignment restriction so each resource is allocated to a single agent, reducing joint actions from O(2^(nr)) to O(n^r), and solve the restricted program while keeping all unilateral-deviation incentive constraints.
result: They prove the restricted feasible set equals the convex hull of chance-constrained pure Nash equilibria in the exact-one set, giving a necessary and sufficient nonemptiness condition, plus a sufficient condition for preserving all unrestricted pure equilibria; a vertiport corridor experiment shows a 99.81% median runtime reduction with equivalent coordination performance.
conclusion: The restriction yields a provably sound and substantially faster formulation for chance-constrained correlated equilibria in exclusive resource-assignment settings, demonstrated on an air-mobility coordination scenario.

title: Gap Entropy And Almost Instance-Wise Optimal Best-Arm Identification
authors: Jiarui Yao, Jiaxi Zhao, Xiangxin Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13703v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the best-arm identification problem, we are given [MATH] stochastic arms with unknown means and wish to identify the arm with the largest mean with probability at least [MATH], using as few samples as possible. We consider independent Gaussian rewards with unit variance and means in [MATH]. Chen and Li [2016] conjectured that the instance-wise sample complexity of this problem is characterized by the gap entropy, up to an additive term arising from the two-arm problem. In this paper, we resolve their gap-entropy and almost instance-wise optimality conjectures. For an instance [MATH], let [MATH] be the gap between the largest and the [MATH]-th largest mean, let [MATH], and let Ent[MATH] denote the entropy of the normalized complexities of its dyadic gap groups. For every [MATH], we show that the order-oblivious instance-wise lower bound is [MATH] We also give a single [MATH]-correct algorithm with expected sample complexity [MATH] without prior knowledge of the gaps. Our lower bound removes the dyadic-gap and monotonicity restrictions of previous work, and our upper bound removes the additional polylogarithmic factor multiplying the two-arm term. Thus, a single algorithm attains the instance-wise lower bound up to an additive two-arm term. The main theorems have been formalized and proved in Lean 4.
