motivation: Best-arm identification is a core problem in sequential decision making and statistics, and prior work conjectured that gap entropy characterizes instance-wise sample complexity up to an additive two-arm term.
method: The authors prove an order-oblivious instance-wise lower bound based on gap entropy and construct a single algorithm achieving expected sample complexity matching this bound, with formal verification in Lean 4.
result: They remove dyadic-gap and monotonicity restrictions from previous lower bounds and eliminate the polylogarithmic factor in the upper bound, showing a single algorithm attains the lower bound up to an additive two-arm term.
conclusion: The gap-entropy and almost instance-wise optimality conjectures are resolved, providing tight characterization of sample complexity for best-arm identification.

title: When Malicious Instructions Persist: Persistent Memory Poisoning Attack On Harness-Based Agents
authors: Shuhuai Huang, Jingfeng Zhang, Hong Jia
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13889v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Harness design has transformed the development of LLM-based agents by integrating memory, tool use, and runtime control. However, this design also introduces security and privacy risks because malicious instructions from external sources may be written into persistent memory and persist across sessions. To study this risk, we propose PMPA, a Persistent Memory Poisoning Attack against harness-based agents. PMPA embeds malicious instructions into benign external sources and induces the victim agent to write them into persistent memory without directly accessing to the agent framework. Once stored, the poisoned memory can be retrieved in later sessions, triggering additional malicious actions and causing privacy leakage. We evaluate PMPA on OpenClaw and Claude Code across different backbone LLMs, input modalities, and trigger scenarios. Across all settings, PMPA achieves average Injection Success Rate (ISR) and Cross-session Attack Success Rate (C-ASR) of 73.7%/ 55.5% on OpenClaw and 66.9%/ 81.7% on Claude Code, while preserving benign task performance on both systems. We further evaluate a targeted prompt-level defense and find that it can reduce memory injection in many settings, but provides limited protection once the persistent memory has been poisoned.
tldr: The paper introduces PMPA, a persistent memory poisoning attack that causes malicious instructions to be written into and retrieved from LLM agent memory across sessions.
motivation: Harness-based LLM agents integrate persistent memory, tool use, and runtime control, creating a security risk where external malicious instructions can survive across sessions without direct framework access.
method: PMPA embeds malicious instructions into benign external sources to induce the victim agent to store them in persistent memory, then evaluates attack success against OpenClaw and Claude Code across backbones, modalities, and triggers.
result: PMPA achieves average ISR/C-ASR of 73.7%/55.5% on OpenClaw and 66.9%/81.7% on Claude Code while preserving benign performance; prompt-level defense reduces injection but offers limited protection after poisoning.
conclusion: Persistent memory in harness-based agents is vulnerable to cross-session poisoning, and prompt-level defenses are insufficient once memory has been compromised.

title: Beam Squint And Aperture--Bandwidth Limitations In Wideband RIS-Assisted THz Links
authors: Waqas Khalid, Chiew Foong Kwong, David Chieng, Qianyu Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.14037v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper analyzes the ergodic rate of a wideband reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted terahertz link under beam squint and finite-resolution phase control. Independent Rayleigh fading on the two RIS-assisted hops produces double-Rayleigh cascaded amplitudes. Exact second- and fourth-order channel moments are derived by incorporating the frequency-dependent array response and phase-quantization errors. Moment matching then provides a Gamma approximation for the received power on each subcarrier and a tractable closed-form approximation for the wideband ergodic rate. A first-null bandwidth approximation characterizes the aperture--bandwidth limitation of frequency-flat RIS control. Monte Carlo simulations validate the analytical framework.
tldr: This paper derives closed-form approximations for the wideband ergodic rate of a RIS-assisted terahertz link subject to beam squint and finite-resolution phase quantization, using double-Rayleigh moment matching and a first-null bandwidth characterization.
motivation: Wideband terahertz links assisted by reconfigurable intelligent surfaces suffer from beam squint and aperture-bandwidth limits because frequency-flat phase control cannot compensate across the band; a tractable analytical rate model is needed to quantify these impairments.
method: Exact second- and fourth-order channel moments are computed by including the frequency-dependent array response and phase-quantization errors, then Gamma moment matching yields per-subcarrier received-power approximations and a closed-form ergodic rate, validated by Monte Carlo simulation.
result: The analysis quantifies how beam squint, phase quantization, and finite aperture bandwidth degrade the wideband ergodic rate, with the first-null bandwidth approximation capturing the frequency-flat RIS control limitation.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides a tractable tool for assessing and designing wideband RIS-assisted THz systems under practical beam-squint and quantization constraints.

title: The Deception Delta: Adversarial Evaluation Of LLM-Based Smart Contract Bytecode Forensics
authors: Timo Schefold
abstract: ArXiv:2609.14098v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used in blockchain forensic investigations to interpret unverified smart contract bytecode. Their robustness has not been systematically tested against contracts adversarially designed to mislead analysis. We evaluate 22 frontier models on 13 purpose-built contracts (9 deception vectors, 4 controls) across six prompt strategies, yielding 8,528 analyzable non-refusal runs against contracts with EVM-verified ground truth. A calibrated LLM-as-judge pipeline, supported by two judge-independent metrics and 50 human gold-standard labels, shows that adversarial deception reduces drain detection by 20.0 percentage points (95% CI: [17.2, 22.8]) relative to functionally matched controls. Structural camouflage via multi-hop call chains, XOR-masked selectors, and storage-loaded drain parameters resists detection across nearly all models. Beyond non-detection, we identify rationalization: models correctly describe the hidden drain mechanism but accept the contract's deceptive framing and dismiss it as benign, yielding positive but incorrect evidence of safety. Simple guard instructions provide no aggregate benefit and destabilize individual models in both directions. Structural deception is largely insensitive across the six tested prompt strategies, more consistent with a capability limitation than with a simple prompting problem. Only five models from two providers exceed 50% detection. Under our single-shot, raw-bytecode-only protocol, current LLMs are not reliable standalone forensic tools. Our central claim does not extend to multi-turn, tool-augmented, source-aware, or decompiler-in-the-loop workflows; a source-code boundary check is reported as an explicit subset analysis rather than as part of the main evaluation.
tldr: This paper adversarially evaluates 22 large language models on their ability to detect deceptive smart contract bytecode, finding that structural deception substantially reduces forensic detection rates and causes models to rationalize hidden drains as benign.
motivation: LLMs are increasingly deployed for blockchain forensic investigations, yet their robustness against adversarially crafted contracts designed to mislead analysis has not been systematically tested.
method: The authors evaluate 22 frontier models on 13 purpose-built contracts (9 deception vectors, 4 controls) across six prompt strategies, producing 8,528 non-refusal runs with EVM-verified ground truth, and use a calibrated LLM-as-judge pipeline with independent metrics and human gold-standard labels.
result: Adversarial deception reduces drain detection by 20.0 percentage points relative to controls, with structural camouflage (multi-hop call chains, XOR-masked selectors, storage-loaded parameters) resisting detection across nearly all models; simple guard instructions provide no aggregate benefit.
conclusion: Current LLMs are not reliable standalone forensic tools under single-shot, raw-bytecode-only conditions, and the observed failures are more consistent with a capability limitation than a prompting problem.

title: On The Complexity Of Finding Fixed Points For Set-Valued Contractions
authors: Pucheng Xiong Emmanouil-Vasileios Vlatakis-Gkaragkounis
abstract: ArXiv:2609.14101v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the computational complexity of finding fixed points for set-valued contractions. We first formulate a computational problem for Nadler's fixed-point theorem: Projected-Nadler, and prove that it is [MATH]-complete by showing its equivalence to Continuous-LocalOpt. We then establish a stronger converse for Nadler's fixed point theorem that can be applied as a tool to analyze the convergence rate of set-valued basic iteration procedure. Finally, we reduce large-margin triplet stationarity problem to Projected-Nadler. Together with its [MATH]-hardness introduced in [arXiv:2509.16898], this yields [MATH]-completeness of large-margin triplet stationarity.
tldr: The paper studies the computational complexity of finding fixed points of set-valued contractions, proving Projected-Nadler is complete for a continuous-local-optimization class and deriving complexity results for large-margin triplet stationarity.
motivation: Fixed-point theorems such as Nadler's guarantee existence of fixed points for set-valued contractions, but the computational cost of actually finding them is not well understood.
method: The authors formulate a search problem called Projected-Nadler, show its equivalence to Continuous-LocalOpt to establish completeness, prove a stronger converse of Nadler's theorem for convergence-rate analysis, and reduce a large-margin triplet stationarity problem to Projected-Nadler.
result: Projected-Nadler is shown complete for the relevant complexity class, and combined with prior hardness results this yields completeness of the large-margin triplet stationarity problem.
conclusion: The work provides a complexity-theoretic characterization of fixed-point computation for set-valued contractions, with implications for convergence analysis of set-valued iteration schemes.

title: H-integrable Solutions To 2d Dimensional Canonical Systems
authors: Keshav Raj Acharya
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13208v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we study [MATH]-dimensional canonical systems with positive semidefinite Hamiltonians [MATH] satisfying [MATH]. We first establish that every such system possesses at least one nontrivial [MATH]-integrable solution, ensuring the existence of solutions whose energy with respect to [MATH] remains finite. We then show that the space of all [MATH]-integrable solutions has dimension at most [MATH].
tldr: The paper studies two-dimensional canonical systems with positive semidefinite Hamiltonians and proves the existence of a nontrivial H-integrable solution, along with a bound on the dimension of the solution space.
motivation: Canonical systems are a central object in the spectral theory of differential equations, and understanding integrable solutions is important for their classification and analysis.
method: The author uses methods from the theory of differential equations and functional analysis to establish existence and dimension bounds for H-integrable solutions.
result: Every such canonical system has at least one nontrivial H-integrable solution, and the space of all H-integrable solutions has dimension at most two.
conclusion: These results provide structural information about canonical systems and contribute to the mathematical theory of differential equations, but they are not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Preconditioned Three-Term Conjugate Gradient Framework For Nonconvex Finite Minimax Problems
authors: Wenzhe Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a hyperbolic-majorization preconditioned three-term nonlinear conjugate-gradient framework for nonconvex finite minimax optimization. An analytic symmetric positive definite metric is derived from a global quadratic majorization of the hyperbolic smoothing model and is used simultaneously as a curvature absorber, a preconditioner, and the line-search energy metric. With the displacement \(s_{k-1}\) fixed and a variable curvature response \(b_k\), an enhanced three-term direction is introduced together with an adaptive parameter \(\mu_k^\star\) that is maximal under the requirement that the baseline worst-case metric-energy constant be preserved. The resulting framework yields a Dai--Liao-type conjugacy relation, enhanced sufficient descent, a smoothing-parameter-uniform Armijo lower bound, fixed-smoothing global first-order convergence and complexity, and Clarke-stationary accumulation points under continuation.
tldr: The paper develops a preconditioned three-term conjugate-gradient framework for nonconvex finite minimax optimization using a hyperbolic-majorization metric.
motivation: Nonconvex minimax problems are important in optimization and machine learning, but standard methods often lack strong convergence guarantees and efficient curvature handling.
method: The authors derive a symmetric positive definite metric from global quadratic majorization of a hyperbolic smoothing model, using it as a preconditioner, curvature absorber, and line-search energy metric within an enhanced three-term conjugate-gradient direction.
result: They establish a Dai-Liao-type conjugacy relation, enhanced sufficient descent, a smoothing-parameter-uniform Armijo lower bound, global first-order convergence and complexity, and Clarke-stationary accumulation points under continuation.
conclusion: The framework provides a theoretically grounded optimization algorithm for nonconvex minimax problems, but it has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: SkillAtlas: An Attack Trace Library For Agent Skills
authors: Yuxin Tian, Zenghao Duan, Liang Pang, Zhiyi Yin, Xueqi Cheng
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13353v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent skills are reusable units for language-model agents, but their risks emerge through model decisions, user context, tool calls, and execution feedback rather than through stable signatures or a single sandbox run. Existing static, dynamic, and benchmark-style evaluations rarely preserve public evidence that can be inspected, searched, and reused. We present SkillAtlas, a hosted attack trace library that converts private agent-skill security report bundles into reviewed, redacted, and searchable public cases. The library contains 3,014 cases, 6,589 traces, 151,131 steps, 233 affected skills, and 8 risk categories; 42.5% of successful cases first become successful after a non-success initial round, and trajectory-grounded labels improve pre-execution guard accuracy to 0.770.
tldr: SkillAtlas is a hosted library of redacted attack traces for language-model agent skills, compiling 3,014 cases and 6,589 traces across 8 risk categories.
motivation: Agent skills introduce security risks that emerge through model decisions, user context, tool calls, and execution feedback, but existing evaluations rarely provide reusable public evidence that can be inspected and searched.
method: The authors convert private agent-skill security report bundles into reviewed, redacted, and searchable public cases, structuring them as attack traces with trajectory-grounded labels.
result: The library contains 3,014 cases, 6,589 traces, 151,131 steps, 233 affected skills, and 8 risk categories; 42.5% of successful cases first become successful after a non-success initial round, and trajectory-grounded labels improve pre-execution guard accuracy to 0.770.
conclusion: SkillAtlas provides a reusable attack trace resource for analyzing and guarding agent-skill security, though it is outside the scope of quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Who Wrote This? Turing, Total Variation, And The Mathematics Of AI-Text Detection
authors: Santiago Schnell
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13660v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: What can a finished text reveal about the process that produced it? Drawing on Turing's imitation game and statistical decision theory, this article examines the limits of AI-text detection as an inference from a completed object to an unobserved history. For two known source distributions with equal prior probabilities, a standard identity gives the minimum average classification error as half their probability overlap. This overlap is one minus their total variation distance. Perfect detection therefore requires nonoverlapping distributions; useful discrimination does not. In practice, the problem is harder: human and machine writing form changing families of distributions, posterior probabilities depend on base rates, and ``AI-written'' becomes ambiguous when people and software contribute to the same text. Turing's interrogator can ask another question; a detector restricted to finished prose cannot. Distinguishability, source attribution, authentication, and compliance are different inferential tasks. The paper's own documented human-AI provenance shows what a production history can reveal that a binary label cannot.
tldr: The paper uses statistical decision theory and total variation distance to analyze fundamental limits of AI-text detection from finished text.
motivation: AI-text detection is often framed as a binary classification problem, but the author argues it is better understood as an inference from a completed text to its unobserved production history, drawing on Turing's imitation game.
method: For two known source distributions with equal priors, the minimum average classification error is half their probability overlap, which equals one minus the total variation distance; the paper also discusses practical complications such as changing distributions, base rates, and mixed human-AI provenance.
result: Perfect detection requires nonoverlapping distributions, while useful discrimination does not; in practice, human and machine writing form changing families of distributions and 'AI-written' becomes ambiguous when both contribute.
conclusion: Distinguishability, source attribution, authentication, and compliance are distinct inferential tasks, and documented provenance can reveal more than a binary label.

title: Decoupling Evidence Sources In Paraconsistent Logic: A Generalized PAL2v Framework For Educational Assessment
authors: Arthur Nakamura, David Drummond, Welbert Pereira, Gustavo Lahr, Kaique Matias de Andrade Roberto
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13284v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Paraconsistent Annotated Logic with two values (PAL2v) annotates a proposition with a pair [MATH] of degrees of favorable and unfavorable evidence, drawn from a bilattice whose four extreme points are the values of Belnap and Dunn. In applications, however, the second coordinate is almost always taken to be the complement of the first, and several such annotations are then fused. We show that this practice determines the sign of the degree of contradiction in advance, independently of the data: for aggregation functions [MATH] and [MATH] the fused degree of contradiction equals [MATH], where [MATH] is the De Morgan dual of [MATH], so that it vanishes identically when the two are dual, and has a constant sign otherwise. In particular the componentwise minimum used throughout the literature yields only consistent annotations, and the conjunction of annotated logic only exact ones; five of the twelve logical states, contradiction among them, are essentially unreachable by construction. We also give a decision procedure for the twelve states that is provably total, in place of the inequality lists in current use, which assign two states to about half of the non-extreme region. We then propose a construction in which the two coordinates are computed from disjoint families of evidence, show that every logical state is attainable. Educational assessment provides a natural instance, since summative and formative instruments are institutionally distinct: mapping examinations to [MATH] and disengagement to [MATH] makes the degree of contradiction equal to the gap between what a student demonstrates and what that student invests. Simulations over three cohort profiles illustrate the classification.
tldr: The paper shows that common PAL2v annotation practices predetermine the sign of contradiction and proposes computing the two evidence coordinates from disjoint sources to make all logical states attainable, with an application to educational assessment.
motivation: In paraconsistent annotated logic applications, the second evidence coordinate is almost always taken as the complement of the first, which artificially restricts the reachable logical states and undermines the meaning of contradiction.
method: The authors analyze aggregation functions on the Belnap-Dunn bilattice, derive the form of the fused contradiction degree, provide a total decision procedure for the twelve logical states, and construct a framework using disjoint evidence families, illustrated by simulations over three cohort profiles.
result: They prove that the fused degree of contradiction equals a function involving the De Morgan dual of the aggregation, that componentwise minimum yields only consistent annotations and conjunction only exact ones, leaving five states unreachable, and that their decoupled construction attains every logical state.
conclusion: Decoupling evidence sources generalizes PAL2v and enables meaningful representation of contradiction, which in educational assessment can quantify the gap between demonstrated performance and student investment.

title: PriMobiBench: Characterizing Visual Privacy Leakage In VLM-Driven Mobile Gui Agents
authors: Qihang Cen, Tianshuo Cong, Da Song, Xinlei He, Jiaxing Song, Ke Xu, Qi Li
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13873v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mobile GUI agents increasingly rely on Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to automate smartphone tasks by interpreting screenshot streams. However, this design introduces serious and underexplored privacy risks, including direct leakage of sensitive on-screen information and unintended user profiling. The absence of standardized benchmarks makes it difficult to quantify these risks in realistic mobile agent workflows. To address this gap, we propose PriMobiBench, the first benchmark for systematically evaluating privacy leakage and visual profiling in screenshot-driven mobile agents. It provides a unified pipeline for data generation, agent trajectory construction, and multi-model evaluation. We also introduce MobiLeak, a dataset of execution traces from 16 apps, covering 25 privacy attributes with 2,960 embedded privacy instances. Our results reveal substantial risks: (1) VLMs can directly extract sensitive information with up to 82.5% success rate; (2) beyond explicit leakage, they can infer user profiles from aggregated visual evidence with approximately 70% success. We further propose a mitigation that masks privacy-sensitive but task-irrelevant UI elements before cloud processing, reducing profiling success by up to 58% with only approximately 8% performance loss. Overall, our work provides the first systematic benchmark for visual privacy risks in mobile GUI agents, demonstrates that both leakage and profiling are feasible at a highly concerning level, and offers a practical direction for mitigation.
tldr: PriMobiBench is the first benchmark for systematically evaluating visual privacy leakage and user profiling in VLM-driven mobile GUI agents, along with a masking-based mitigation strategy.
motivation: Mobile GUI agents that interpret screenshot streams via Vision-Language Models introduce serious but underexplored privacy risks, and no standardized benchmark exists to quantify them in realistic workflows.
method: The authors build a unified pipeline for data generation, agent trajectory construction, and multi-model evaluation, and introduce MobiLeak, a dataset of execution traces from 16 apps covering 25 privacy attributes with 2,960 embedded privacy instances.
result: VLMs extract sensitive on-screen information with up to 82.5% success and infer user profiles from aggregated visual evidence with about 70% success; a UI-element masking mitigation cuts profiling success by up to 58% at roughly 8% task-performance loss.
conclusion: The work provides the first systematic benchmark showing that both leakage and profiling are feasible at concerning levels in mobile GUI agents and offers a practical masking-based mitigation direction.

title: A High-Throughput Fpga Architecture For Real-Time Tcp-syn Scan Detection
authors: Faisal Saeed, Mohammad Fahad, Ayesha Javaid, Christian Doerr, Muhammad Ali Siddiqi
abstract: ArXiv:2609.14043v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: TCP-SYN port scanning often precedes cyber-attacks, and early detection of scanner fingerprints embedded in packet headers can provide timely intrusion alerts. Existing approaches are either too computationally expensive for line-rate operation or limited to offline analysis. This brief presents a lightweight FPGA architecture for reconfigurable line-rate fingerprint detection, where each fingerprint is compiled into a shallow Boolean LUT tree, enabling parallel evaluation with constant two-cycle latency regardless of fingerprint count, while resource cost grows linearly with fingerprint count. This detection core is decoupled from a MAC-layer frontend that performs streaming field extraction with no frame buffering or higher-layer state, allowing deployment across different line rates by modifying only the frontend. A Python framework automatically compiles Boolean expressions into synthesizable HDL, eliminating manual RTL changes. For TCP-SYN port-scan fingerprint detection, the architecture uses approximately 0.5% LUTs at 10 Gbps on a Versal VCK190 for 18 deployed fingerprints, with capacity for over 2,000 concurrent fingerprints, and under 2.5% on a Virtex-6 at 1 Gbps, with a detection latency of 10 ns at both rates, three to four orders of magnitude below typical per-packet processing latency in software intrusion-detection systems. The system was cross-validated against a software re-implementation on an 8-hour production packet trace, confirming detection correctness with zero false positives/negatives.
tldr: The paper presents a lightweight, reconfigurable FPGA architecture that detects TCP-SYN port-scan fingerprints at line rate by compiling Boolean fingerprint expressions into shallow LUT trees with constant two-cycle latency.
motivation: TCP-SYN port scanning typically precedes cyber-attacks, so early detection of scanner fingerprints in packet headers can provide timely intrusion alerts, but existing approaches are either too computationally expensive for line-rate operation or limited to offline analysis.
method: Each fingerprint is compiled by a Python framework into synthesizable HDL implementing a shallow Boolean LUT tree, enabling parallel evaluation with constant two-cycle latency and linearly growing resource cost; this detection core is decoupled from a MAC-layer streaming frontend that performs field extraction without frame buffering or higher-layer state.
result: On a Versal VCK190 at 10 Gbps the design uses ~0.5% of LUTs for 18 fingerprints with capacity for over 2,000, and under 2.5% on a Virtex-6 at 1 Gbps, achieving 10 ns detection latency (three to four orders of magnitude below software IDS per-packet latency) with zero false positives/negatives verified against a software re-implementation on an 8-hour production packet trace.
conclusion: The architecture offers a scalable, line-rate, hardware-accelerated approach to network intrusion fingerprint detection, but it is a classical networking/security engineering contribution with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Data-Driven Cohesive Zone Modeling Within The Generalized Standard Materials Framework
authors: Sida Hao, Jinkyo Han, Bahador Bahmani
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13629v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cohesive zone models are widely used to describe fracture and interfacial failure, yet most formulations prescribe problem-specific analytical traction-separation laws together with phenomenological rules for unloading and reloading, leading to specialized models for different cohesive behaviors. This work develops a unified learnable cohesive formulation within the generalized standard materials framework, in which the response is generated from learned constitutive functions while the underlying thermodynamic structure remains fixed. The surface free energy is decomposed into active and contact contributions, and irreversible damage evolution is governed by a learned mode-dependent damage resistance. The active energy is represented by an input-convex neural network, while the inverse damage resistance is represented by a monotone neural network. Convexity, monotonicity, normalization, and damage irreversibility are incorporated directly into the constitutive representation. Direct parameterization of the inverse resistance yields an explicit damage update and avoids local nonlinear inversion during constitutive evaluation. Material-point studies show that the formulation can represent qualitatively distinct cohesive responses, including plateaus, extended softening tails, irregular softening, nonlinear unloading, distinct Mode I and Mode II behaviors, and several classical mixed-mode cohesive laws. The framework therefore replaces law-specific model construction with a single thermodynamically structured representation capable of learning cohesive responses of broad functional complexity from data.
tldr: This paper develops a data-driven cohesive zone modeling framework within the generalized standard materials framework, using neural networks to learn traction-separation laws while preserving thermodynamic structure.
motivation: Cohesive zone models typically require problem-specific analytical traction-separation laws and phenomenological unloading/reloading rules, which limits their generality and requires specialized formulations for different cohesive behaviors.
method: The authors decompose surface free energy into active and contact contributions and learn a mode-dependent damage resistance using an input-convex neural network for active energy and a monotone neural network for inverse damage resistance, enforcing convexity, monotonicity, normalization, and damage irreversibility directly in the constitutive representation.
result: Material-point studies demonstrate the formulation can represent qualitatively distinct cohesive responses, including plateaus, extended softening tails, irregular softening, nonlinear unloading, distinct Mode I and Mode II behaviors, and several classical mixed-mode cohesive laws.
conclusion: The framework replaces law-specific model construction with a single thermodynamically structured representation capable of learning cohesive responses of broad functional complexity from data.

title: Relevant Sampling Of Non-decaying Signals In Orlicz And Mixed-norm Orlicz Spaces Defined On A Locally Compact Group
authors: S. Sivananthan Sarthak Raj
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13732v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the sampling problem for non-decaying signals defined on a locally compact group. The signals are modeled as elements of suitable subspaces of weighted Orlicz and weighted mixed-norm Orlicz spaces, thereby allowing controlled growth at infinity. Our principal focus is on image spaces of idempotent integral operators. Under suitable oscillation estimates on the associated integral kernels, we establish deterministic sampling theorems that guarantee stable reconstruction from pointwise samples. We further prove an average sampling result in the same setting. In addition, we prove random sampling theorems for functions whose norm is essentially concentrated on a compact subset of the group. In particular, we show that, with high probability, sampling is possible from [MATH] randomly chosen sample points, where [MATH] denotes the compact set on which the signal, belonging to Orlicz space, is essentially norm concentrated. In the same spirit, a random sampling result is proved for signals in mixed-norm Orlicz space. As applications of the abstract theory, we obtain sampling theorems for weighted shift-invariant spaces and Orlicz modulation spaces.
tldr: The paper develops deterministic and random sampling theorems for non-decaying signals in weighted Orlicz and mixed-norm Orlicz spaces on locally compact groups.
motivation: Sampling theory for signals with controlled growth at infinity is important for extending classical reconstruction results beyond decaying signals and standard Lp spaces.
method: The authors model signals in idempotent integral operator image spaces, impose oscillation estimates on integral kernels, and prove stable reconstruction from pointwise and average samples, with additional random sampling results for norm-concentrated signals.
result: They establish deterministic sampling theorems, an average sampling result, and random sampling guarantees from O(1) chosen points for signals essentially concentrated on a compact set, with applications to weighted shift-invariant spaces and Orlicz modulation spaces.
conclusion: The work provides a general harmonic-analysis framework for sampling non-decaying signals in Orlicz-type spaces on locally compact groups, extending sampling theory to broader function spaces.

title: Last-Iterate Performance Of Gradient Descent And Relaxed Proximal Point Via $s$-Composability
authors: Salah Chikhi
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13765v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The notion of s-composability was introduced to compose optimized stepsize schedules while preserving sharp guarantees. We show that the same joint potential has a second use: it can serve directly as a certificate of sharp last-iterate performance. We develop this viewpoint for constant and silver schedules. For the constant schedule, we prove the s-composability statement posed as an open question by Grimmer et al. (2025), at every finite horizon, through an explicit nonnegative smooth-convex interpolation certificate. The result identifies the unique constant stepsize minimizing the worst-case final gradient norm of smooth convex gradient descent under an initial-distance bound, thereby proving the optimal stepsize, value, and uniqueness predicted by Conjecture 3 of Taylor et al. (2017) without resolving its full worst-case curve. Through the Moreau envelope, the same constant is also the unique constant relaxation minimizing the worst-case final residual of relaxed proximal point. More generally, for every positive s-composable schedule, we determine the exact worst-case final proximal objective-gap constant and give a matching one-dimensional example. Applying this result to the already s-composable original silver schedule yields its exact last-iterate objective-gap constant, closing a question left open by Wang et al. (2025).
tldr: The paper uses s-composability to certify sharp last-iterate performance of gradient descent and relaxed proximal point methods, resolving open questions about optimal stepsizes and worst-case constants.
motivation: The s-composability framework was previously used to compose optimized stepsize schedules while preserving sharp guarantees, but its potential as a direct certificate for last-iterate performance remained unexplored.
method: The authors analyze the joint potential underlying s-composability, constructing nonnegative smooth-convex interpolation certificates for constant and silver schedules, and use the Moreau envelope to connect gradient descent with relaxed proximal point.
result: For the constant schedule, they prove an open s-composability statement, identify the unique constant stepsize minimizing worst-case final gradient norm, and confirm conjectures from Taylor et al. (2017); for every positive s-composable schedule, they determine the exact worst-case final proximal objective-gap constant and apply it to the silver schedule.
conclusion: The work establishes s-composability as a versatile tool for certifying last-iterate optimality, answering open problems and closing a question left open by Wang et al. (2025) for the silver schedule.

title: Cyclotomic Expansions Of Colored $SU(n)$ Invariants Of Two-strand Torus Knots And Bailey Transforms
authors: Chuwen Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13766v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Habiro's cyclotomic expansion of the colored Jones polynomial has a higher rank analogue conjectured by Chen--Liu--Zhu for colored [MATH] invariants. We prove this conjecture for torus knots [MATH] and give a Bailey theoretic realization of the cyclotomic coefficients. For [MATH] and [MATH], the colored [MATH] invariants admit an expansion $[MATH][MATH]H_m^{(n,p)}(q)\in\mathbb Z[q^{\pm1}][MATH]N[MATH]T(2,2p+1)[MATH]{}_6\phi_5[MATH]q[MATH]SU(n)[MATH]T(2,2p+1)$.
tldr: The paper proves a higher-rank cyclotomic expansion conjecture for colored SU(n) invariants of two-strand torus knots and interprets the coefficients via Bailey transforms.
motivation: Habiro's cyclotomic expansion of the colored Jones polynomial has a conjectured higher-rank analogue for colored SU(n) invariants due to Chen--Liu--Zhu, which lacked a proof for torus knots.
method: The author proves the conjecture for torus knots T(2,2p+1) and realizes the cyclotomic coefficients through Bailey's transform machinery and q-hypergeometric identities.

title: Interior-point Proximal Methods For Nonsmooth Optimization In Hilbert Spaces With Cone-ordered Constraints
authors: Alberto de Marchi Behzad Azmi
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13813v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study an inexact interior-point method for nonsmooth, nonconvex optimization problems with conic inequality constraints. The objective function is given by the sum of a smooth, possibly nonconvex term and a convex, possibly nonsmooth term with a computable proximal mapping. The constraints are formulated by means of an order cone in a Banach lattice. This setting covers finite-dimensional nonsmooth nonlinear problems with componentwise constraints as well as infinite-dimensional PDE-constrained optimization problems with pointwise state constraints. The method is based on barrier-regularized subproblems, which are solved inexactly by a proximal-gradient method. We consider logarithmic and power-type barriers and derive the differentiability and curvature estimates needed for the convergence and complexity analysis. Under standard constraint qualifications, we establish KKT-type optimality conditions for the original problem and show that the primal iterates and barrier-induced multipliers satisfy approximate KKT conditions. For the interior-point scheme, we prove convergence to stationary points and derive bounds on the total number of proximal-gradient iterations needed to reach approximate stationarity. In particular, we show that the total complexity is dominated by the final outer iterations because of the growth of the barrier curvature. In the convex setting, we obtain stronger convergence results: the full sequence converges weakly to a global solution and strongly under a quadratic growth condition. We apply the abstract results to state-constrained semilinear elliptic optimal control problems, for which all assumptions are verified, and to finite-dimensional sparse dictionary-learning problems with nonlinear side constraints. Numerical experiments support the theoretical findings.
tldr: The paper develops an inexact interior-point method for nonsmooth, nonconvex optimization with conic inequality constraints in Banach lattices, with convergence and complexity analysis.
motivation: Nonsmooth nonconvex problems with cone-ordered constraints arise in finite-dimensional componentwise-constrained problems and in infinite-dimensional PDE-constrained optimization, but existing interior-point theory largely targets smooth or finite-dimensional settings.
method: Barrier-regularized subproblems (logarithmic and power-type barriers) are solved inexactly via a proximal-gradient method, with differentiability and curvature estimates derived to support KKT-type optimality and iteration-complexity analysis.
result: The authors prove convergence to stationary points, derive bounds on total proximal-gradient iterations dominated by final outer iterations due to barrier curvature growth, and obtain weak/strong global convergence in the convex case; abstract results are verified on state-constrained semilinear elliptic control and sparse dictionary learning.
conclusion: The framework extends inexact interior-point proximal methods to Hilbert-space cone-ordered nonsmooth problems and is supported by numerical experiments, but it lies entirely within classical optimization theory.

title: CyclOT: Learning Quadratic Optimal Transport Maps Via Synchronized Forward-Backward Interpolants
authors: Shizhou Xu, Jiachen Liu, Shih-Hsin Wang, Stefan Broecker, Yuhao Huang, Bao Wang, Thomas Strohmer
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13892v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the recovery of forward and reverse quadratic optimal-transport maps from unpaired samples in high dimensions. We introduce a bidirectional neural framework in which the learned maps induce forward and backward displacement interpolants, while the training objective combines bidirectional quadratic action, discriminator-restricted Jensen-Shannon endpoint objectives, and two-sided cycle consistency. The construction requires neither precomputed sample pairings nor an explicit convex-potential parameterization. For absolutely continuous probability measures supported on a compact convex set, and under the stated generator-approximation, discriminator-richness, and minimizer-attainment conditions, we prove a population recovery theorem: for every prescribed accuracy, the sum of the corresponding \(L^2\) errors between any global minimizer and the forward and reverse quadratic Brenier maps is below that accuracy, provided the discriminator level is sufficiently large and the annealing action weight becomes sufficiently small. Moreover, the cycle loss is bounded above by \(\lambda W_2^2(\mu_0,\mu_1)\). Complementary results quantify approximate invertibility and show that exact endpoint Jensen-Shannon divergence and cycle consistency control missing target mass and many-to-one map collapse, respectively. Experiments on Swiss roll, MNIST, CelebA, single-cell perturbation data, and chest X-ray images evaluate endpoint fidelity, transport cost, inverse consistency, and the geometry of the induced interpolations.
tldr: The paper introduces CyclOT, a bidirectional neural framework for learning forward and reverse quadratic optimal transport maps from unpaired samples in high dimensions.
motivation: Recovering optimal transport maps without paired samples or explicit convex potential parameterization is challenging, especially in high-dimensional settings.
method: The method combines bidirectional quadratic action, discriminator-restricted Jensen-Shannon endpoint objectives, and two-sided cycle consistency to train neural networks that induce forward and backward displacement interpolants.
result: Under specified conditions, a population recovery theorem guarantees that global minimizers approximate the forward and reverse quadratic Brenier maps in L2 error, with cycle loss bounded by a Wasserstein distance term; experiments on synthetic and real datasets evaluate endpoint fidelity, transport cost, and inverse consistency.
conclusion: CyclOT provides a principled neural approach to quadratic optimal transport map recovery, with theoretical guarantees and empirical validation across diverse domains.

title: Risk Comparison Theorems And Application To Deep Learning Of Diffusion Coefficients
authors: Nakahiro Yoshida Arnaud Gloter
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13898v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the nonparametric estimation of the diffusion matrix in stochastic differential equations featuring multidimensional, strong mixing covariate processes. We propose a flexible statistical framework based on general function classes that does not require a linear basis representation, rendering our results directly applicable to deep neural network estimators. Our approach employs a two-step estimation procedure: constructing a preliminary nonparametric quasi-likelihood estimator and subsequently regularizing it via a [MATH]-H\"older class approximation. We establish general risk comparison theorems between empirical and generalization risks for arbitrary estimators without relying on a specific probabilistic structure of the underlying process. In diffusion matrix learning based on \(n + 1\) observations over the time interval \([0,T]\), the derived upper bounds capture the intrinsic interplay between the \(T\)-rate, associated with the mixing behavior of the covariate process, and the intrinsic \(n\)-rate governing the volatility estimation.
tldr: The paper develops risk comparison theorems for nonparametric estimation of diffusion coefficients using general function classes and deep neural networks.
motivation: Nonparametric estimation of diffusion matrices in stochastic differential equations is challenging, especially with multidimensional strongly mixing covariates, and existing methods often rely on linear basis representations that limit flexibility.
method: A two-step procedure is proposed: first a preliminary nonparametric quasi-likelihood estimator is constructed, then regularized via Hölder class approximation, with general risk comparison theorems between empirical and generalization risks for arbitrary estimators.
result: Upper bounds are derived that capture the interplay between the T-rate from mixing behavior of the covariate process and the intrinsic n-rate governing volatility estimation.
conclusion: The framework is directly applicable to deep neural network estimators and provides a flexible statistical foundation for diffusion matrix learning without requiring linear basis representations.

title: Failure Of Rockafellar's Sum Conjecture Via An Explicit Non-(FPV) Operator
authors: Radu Ioan Bot
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13906v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Building on a construction of Weifeng Yang, we present a simplified counterexample to Rockafellar's sum conjecture on [MATH]. The central observation is geometric: the domain of a maximally monotone operator can have a nonconvex norm closure. In our example, this gives a short proof that the operator is not of type (FPV), which in turn implies the failure of the sum conjecture. We define an explicit operator using geometric series and provide a detailed proof of its maximal monotonicity. The example was developed with assistance from GPT-6 Astra. The purpose is to simplify and explain the construction, not to claim an independent counterexample mechanism.
tldr: The paper gives a simplified explicit counterexample to Rockafellar's sum conjecture using a maximally monotone operator whose domain has nonconvex norm closure and which is not of type (FPV).
motivation: Rockafellar's sum conjecture is a longstanding problem in convex analysis and monotone operator theory, and the work aims to clarify and simplify a prior counterexample construction of Weifeng Yang.
method: The construction defines an explicit maximally monotone operator using geometric series, proves its maximal monotonicity in detail, and uses a geometric observation about the nonconvexity of the norm closure of its domain to show it is not of type (FPV).
result: The operator provides a short proof that the sum conjecture fails, because the non-(FPV) property implies the failure of Rockafellar's sum conjecture.
conclusion: The paper simplifies and explains the counterexample mechanism rather than claiming an independent one, serving as an accessible account of the failure of the sum conjecture.

title: Partitioning-free 3d-ic Floorplanning
authors: Shuo Ren, Rongliang Fu, Libo Shen, Zhen Zhuang, Leilei Jin, Hao Yu, Bei Yu, Tsung-Yi Ho
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13157v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: 3D integration with fine-pitch hybrid bonding offers a promising path to alleviate interconnect bottlenecks in conventional two-dimensional (2D) ICs, yet efficient 3D floorplanning remains challenging due to the enlarged solution space and non-uniform inter-die communication latency. Existing methods either extend 2D representations into 3D, leading to combinatorial complexity, or adopt partitioning-first pipelines that fix block-to-die assignments early and hinder joint optimization of floorplan, die assignment, and vertical connectivity. In this work, we present , a partitioning-free 3D floorplanning framework that directly optimizes a native 3D floorplan. formulates a unified objective that couples interconnect cost with a cycles-per-instruction (CPI)-derived latency term to capture the system-level impact of face-to-face (F2F) bonding. Algorithmically, it combines an SDP-based 3D global embedding with a dynamic-programming refinement for die assignment, followed by 2D continuous refinement with practical design constraints. {Experiments on the GSRC and ATPlace benchmark suites show that consistently achieves strong wirelength and CPI quality against state-of-the-art 3D floorplanners. On GSRC, it reduces total wirelength by up to about [MATH] (and by [MATH]--[MATH] on average) over competing 3D-native floorplanners, and its dynamic-programming die-assignment stage further improves CPI by [MATH]--[MATH], while maintaining competitive runtime on instances of up to a few hundred blocks.}.
tldr: The paper introduces a partitioning-free 3D-IC floorplanning framework that jointly optimizes floorplan, die assignment, and vertical connectivity using an SDP-based global embedding and dynamic-programming refinement.
motivation: 3D integration with fine-pitch hybrid bonding can alleviate interconnect bottlenecks, but existing 3D floorplanners either expand the solution space combinatorially or fix block-to-die assignments early, preventing joint optimization.
method: The framework formulates a unified objective coupling interconnect cost with a CPI-derived latency term, and combines semidefinite-programming-based 3D global embedding, dynamic-programming die assignment, and 2D continuous refinement under practical constraints.
result: Experiments on GSRC and ATPlace benchmarks show wirelength reductions up to about [MATH] over state-of-the-art 3D-native floorplanners, CPI improvements of [MATH]–[MATH] from the die-assignment stage, and competitive runtime for instances up to a few hundred blocks.
conclusion: A partitioning-free approach can improve 3D floorplanning quality by jointly optimizing layout and die assignment, offering better wirelength and system-level CPI compared to existing methods.

title: Ei-ddlgn: Efficient Encrypted Inference With Deep Differentiable Logic Gate Networks Under Tfhe
authors: Mahmoud Y. M. Yassin, Mahmoud Abdelhafeez Sayed, Mostafa Taha
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13636v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Privacy-preserving inference via Torus Fully Homomorphic Encryption (TFHE) provides strong protection for sensitive data in outsourced deep learning applications. However, most TFHE-compatible neural network frameworks remain based on arithmetic neural architectures, resulting in high inference latency due to programmable bootstrapping (PBS), accumulator growth, and circuit bit-width sensitivity. In this work, we investigate Deep Differentiable Logic Gate Networks (DDLGNs) as a Boolean-native alternative for encrypted inference under TFHE. Because DDLGNs learn Boolean computations directly and discretize into fixed logic gate networks, their inference procedure is naturally aligned with TFHE's Boolean execution model and avoids arithmetic accumulation in hidden layers. We present EI-DDLGN, the first in-depth study of TFHE-based DDLGN inference, and characterize how encrypted execution cost depends on model size, learned Boolean-function distribution, and propagated wire status. We also introduce Model-Fixed-Wire PBS Bypass (MFW-PBS Bypass), a semantics-preserving execution strategy that eliminates unnecessary PBS operations without modifying the learned network topology. Evaluations across 72 depth-width configurations on MNIST, FashionMNIST, and UCI Phishing show that DDLGNs constitute an efficient alternative to arithmetic TFHE inference, achieving substantially improved accuracy-latency trade-offs. Notably, on MNIST, EI-DDLGN-Small matches the accuracy of QAT-FCNN-4 while reducing encrypted inference latency by 13.4x. Our implementation is available at [URL].
tldr: EI-DDLGN studies TFHE-based encrypted inference using deep differentiable logic gate networks, achieving better accuracy-latency trade-offs than arithmetic neural architectures.
motivation: Most TFHE-compatible neural network frameworks rely on arithmetic architectures, causing high latency from programmable bootstrapping and accumulator growth.
method: The authors investigate Boolean-native Deep Differentiable Logic Gate Networks (DDLGNs) for TFHE encrypted inference and introduce Model-Fixed-Wire PBS Bypass to eliminate unnecessary bootstrapping operations.
result: Across 72 depth-width configurations on MNIST, FashionMNIST, and UCI Phishing, EI-DDLGN improves accuracy-latency trade-offs; notably, EI-DDLGN-Small matches QAT-FCNN-4 accuracy while reducing encrypted inference latency by 13.4x on MNIST.
conclusion: DDLGNs provide an efficient Boolean-native alternative to arithmetic TFHE inference for privacy-preserving deep learning.

title: Online Fair Division: Pushing The Frontier Of Approximate Proportionality
authors: Ankang Sun Yingjian Du
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13650v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Online fair division captures allocation problems in which indivisible resources arrive over time and must be assigned before future resources are known. Understanding what fairness remains achievable when allocation decisions are immediate and irrevocable is a fundamental question in this setting. We study deterministic online allocation among [MATH] agents with nonnegative additive valuations, where the number of goods is unknown and the adversary can adapt to previous allocation decisions. We focus on proportionality up to one good (PROP1) and examine how advance future information affects the achievable guarantees. In the setting without additional information, we answer an open question in Choo et al. that asks whether a nontrivial deterministic approximation for PROP1 can be obtained. In particular, we present a deterministic algorithm that guarantees [MATH]-PROP1, where [MATH] is the number of goods. Moreover, we complement this result by showing that, for every fixed [MATH] and all sufficiently large [MATH], every deterministic algorithm has an instance with [MATH] goods on which its PROP1 factor is [MATH]. We also study the setting where the algorithm knows in advance the maximum item value (MIV) for every agent. With MIV information, we give a deterministic algorithm with competitive ratio 1/2, improving the [MATH] guarantee in Choo et al. We also show that no deterministic algorithm can achieve a competitive ratio arbitrarily close to one, even for two agents with exact MIV information.
tldr: This paper studies deterministic online fair division for indivisible goods, establishing new guarantees and lower bounds for proportionality up to one good (PROP1), with and without advance information about maximum item values.
motivation: Online fair division addresses settings where indivisible resources arrive over time and must be allocated immediately and irrevocably, raising the question of what fairness guarantees remain achievable under adversarial arrival orders.
method: The authors design deterministic online allocation algorithms for PROP1, analyze their competitive ratios, and prove impossibility results via adversarial instances; they also consider a setting where the maximum item value (MIV) is known in advance.
result: Without extra information, they give a deterministic algorithm achieving an m-dependent PROP1 approximation and show a matching lower bound for large m; with MIV information, they achieve competitive ratio 1/2 and prove that no deterministic algorithm can approach ratio 1 even for two agents.
conclusion: The work advances the frontier of approximate proportionality in online fair division, resolving an open question and clarifying the power and limits of advance value information.

title: Mechanizing G\"odel's Incompleteness Theorems And Provability Logic
authors: Mashu Noguchi Shogo Saitou
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13780v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We mechanized proof of G\"odel's first and second incompleteness theorems, Solovay's arithmetical completeness theorem of , and related results in the Lean 4 theorem prover.
tldr: The paper formalizes Gödel's incompleteness theorems and provability logic in the Lean 4 proof assistant.
motivation: Mechanizing these foundational metamathematical results provides verified proofs and supports further formalization in proof assistants.
method: The authors use the Lean 4 theorem prover to mechanize proofs of Gödel's first and second incompleteness theorems, Solovay's arithmetical completeness theorem, and related results.
result: They successfully formalize these classical theorems and related provability logic results in Lean 4.
conclusion: This work contributes to the formal verification of mathematical logic but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: GNN-Based Polarforming For Multi-User Miso Short-Packet Urllc Under Imperfect Csi
authors: Zahra Mehrzad, Hamed Aghaei-Karkaj, Rahman Saadat Yeganeh, Kamran Ebrahimi, Mohammad Robat Mili, Symeon Chatzinotas, Ioannis Krikidis
abstract: ArXiv:2609.14006v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates polarization-aware transmission for multi-user multiple-input single-output (MU-MISO) short-packet ultra-reliable low-latency communications (URLLC) under imperfect channel state information (CSI). We consider a system in which the base station (BS) and users are equipped with polarization-reconfigurable antennas that enable adaptive polarization states through controllable polarization coefficients. A multi-objective optimization problem is formulated to jointly maximize the finite-blocklength (FBL) achievable sum rate and minimize the maximum decoding error probability (DEP), subject to transmit-power, latency, reliability, and discrete polarization-control constraints. The resulting multi-objective problem is scalarized using a normalized weighted-sum utility. To enable low-complexity online decision-making, a heterogeneous graph neural network (GNN) is developed to learn the joint mapping from estimated polarized CSI to digital beamforming and transmit/receive polarforming vectors (PFVs) while accounting for the system constraints. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed GNN-based polarforming (PF) framework substantially improves the FBL sum rate while reducing the maximum DEP compared with conventional fixed-polarization schemes, particularly under channel depolarization and imperfect CSI. This highlights the potential of adaptive polarization control for reliable low-latency transmission.
tldr: This paper proposes a heterogeneous graph neural network (GNN) for joint digital beamforming and polarization control in multi-user MISO short-packet URLLC under imperfect CSI.
motivation: Adaptive polarization control can improve reliability and latency in URLLC, but joint optimization under finite blocklength, imperfect CSI, and discrete polarization constraints is challenging.
method: A multi-objective optimization problem maximizing FBL sum rate and minimizing maximum decoding error probability is scalarized, then a GNN learns the mapping from estimated polarized CSI to beamforming and transmit/receive polarforming vectors.
result: Numerical results show that the proposed GNN-based polarforming framework substantially improves FBL sum rate and reduces maximum DEP compared with conventional fixed-polarization schemes, especially under channel depolarization and imperfect CSI.
conclusion: Adaptive polarization control via GNNs is promising for reliable low-latency transmission in MU-MISO URLLC systems.

title: Finite-Mask Gaussian-Process Reconstruction On A Periodic Sensor Ring: Mask-Geometry Dependence, Fourier-Mode Coupling, And Posterior Trace
authors: Jun Tsuzurugi
abstract: ArXiv:2609.14007v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze how an arbitrary observation mask on a finite periodic ring of equally spaced sensors affects the posterior covariance, Fourier-mode coupling, and normalized posterior trace in Gaussian-process reconstruction. Under a rotationally stationary prior and homogeneous independent measurement noise, complete observation gives independent scalar posterior formulas for the Fourier modes. For an arbitrary mask, however, the matrix [MATH] is generally non-diagonal; its off-diagonal entries are finite Fourier components of the realized mask and couple modes in the posterior precision. Consequently, masks with the same unavailable-channel fraction can have different normalized posterior traces because their geometries differ. A dimensionless 64-channel synthetic benchmark illustrates this finite-matrix effect. A circumferential array of equally spaced wall-mounted microphones at a fixed axial station of a circular fan or compressor duct provides one concrete mechanical-engineering interpretation: failed, saturated, corrupted, or dropped-out channels form the observation mask. The analysis is a finite-dimensional reference calculation under the stated rotational-stationarity and common-noise assumptions, not a performance claim for a nonuniform or unequally instrumented operating duct.
tldr: Analyzes how an arbitrary observation mask on a finite periodic sensor ring affects posterior covariance, Fourier-mode coupling, and normalized posterior trace in Gaussian-process reconstruction.
motivation: The paper aims to understand how missing, failed, or corrupted sensor channels influence Gaussian-process reconstruction in periodic sensor arrays, motivated by microphone arrays in circular ducts.
method: It derives posterior precision matrices for arbitrary masks under rotational stationarity and homogeneous noise, showing off-diagonal Fourier components couple modes, and illustrates the effect with a 64-channel synthetic benchmark.
result: Masks with the same unavailable-channel fraction can yield different normalized posterior traces because mask geometry changes Fourier-mode coupling in the posterior precision.
conclusion: The work is a finite-dimensional reference calculation under specific stationarity and noise assumptions, not a performance claim for nonuniform or unequally instrumented operating ducts.

title: Polarforming-Enabled Power-Splitting Swipt: A GNN-Based Optimization Approach
authors: Hamed Aghaei-Karkaj, Kamran Ebrahimi, Zahra Mehrzad, Mohammad Robat Mili, Symeon Chatzinotas, Ioannis Krikidis
abstract: ArXiv:2609.14014v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) is a critical technology for the future of the Internet of Things (IoT). However, ensuring a stable power supply in such networks remains a significant challenge. This work introduces dynamic polarization control as an additional degree of freedom (DoF) in SWIPT systems. We propose a system where both the base station (BS) and the users can adjust their antenna polarization, a technique known as polarforming. In addition, each user device is capable of splitting the incident signal to perform simultaneous information decoding (ID) and energy harvesting (EH). The resulting non-convex optimization, with many coupled variables, is solved using a graph neural network (GNN) that learns the sub-optimal beamforming, polarization, and power-splitting variables. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed GNN-based dynamic polarforming optimization significantly outperforms fixed-polarization schemes, particularly under imperfect channel state information (CSI). Moreover, joint polarforming and GNN-based optimization maintain robust SWIPT performance under both polarization mismatch and imperfect CSI.
tldr: This paper proposes dynamic polarization control (polarforming) for SWIPT systems and uses a graph neural network to jointly optimize beamforming, polarization, and power-splitting variables.
motivation: Stable power supply remains a major challenge for IoT devices relying on simultaneous wireless information and power transfer, and additional degrees of freedom are needed to improve performance under imperfect channel state information.
method: The authors formulate a non-convex optimization problem with coupled variables for joint beamforming, polarization, and power splitting, and solve it using a graph neural network that learns sub-optimal solutions.
result: Simulation results show that the proposed GNN-based dynamic polarforming optimization significantly outperforms fixed-polarization schemes, particularly under imperfect CSI and polarization mismatch.
conclusion: Joint polarforming and GNN-based optimization provides robust SWIPT performance and is a promising approach for future IoT networks.

title: SkillSecurer: Detecting And Patching Prompt-Injection Vulnerabilities In Ai Agent Skills
authors: Donato Mecca, Alberto Verna, Youness Bouchari, Nikhil Jha, Marco Mellia
abstract: ArXiv:2609.14079v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent skills extend AI agents with reusable instructions, scripts, and configuration, but are also open to new attacks to influence an agent's decisions and actions. To address these risks, we present SkillSecurer, a fully agentic framework for generating, detecting, localising, and remediating security risks in agent skills. Its red agent generates context-compatible injections across nine threat types while recording the exact modification; its blue agent analyses complete skill packages, produces grounded evidence, and proposes patches. For controlled instances, a verifier compares findings and patches with the recorded injection, enabling injection-level evaluation. We thoroughly evaluate SkillSecurer by selecting the best backend LLM, comparing it with competitors, and manually cross-validating each evaluation stage. With its best performing backend, SkillSecurer is the only scanner to achieve a 100% injection detection rate. Next, we analyse popular skills from skills.sh, finding latent vulnerabilities in more than 17% of the skills examined. Testing some of those skills, we trigger actual incidents, showing the risks of running unverified skills. Our results show that context-aware LLM analysis can provide reliable injection localisation and actionable remediation beyond skill-level flagging alone.
tldr: SkillSecurer is an agentic framework for detecting, localizing, and patching prompt-injection vulnerabilities in AI agent skills.
motivation: Agent skills are reusable and increasingly adopted, but they introduce new attack surfaces where malicious instructions can influence an AI agent's decisions and actions.
method: The framework uses a red agent to generate nine types of context-compatible injections and a blue agent to analyze full skill packages, provide evidence, and propose patches, with a verifier for controlled evaluation.
result: The best backend achieves 100% injection detection, and scanning popular skills reveals latent vulnerabilities in over 17% of examined skills, with some triggering actual incidents.
conclusion: Context-aware LLM analysis enables reliable injection localization and actionable remediation, improving security beyond simple skill-level flagging.

title: Data-Driven Flutter Suppression Via Hodmd, DMDcand Constrained Mpc
authors: Carlos Mendez
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13459v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work presents an interpretable data-to-control framework for actuator-constrained flutter suppression by combining higher-order dynamic mode decomposition (HODMD), dynamic mode decomposition with control (DMDc), and model predictive control (MPC). The primary case is a pitch-plunge typical section with a trailing-edge flap and rational unsteady aerodynamics. HODMD identifies the dominant frequency and growth rate in subcritical, near-critical, and post-critical regimes from four measured structural channels. With 2% RMS sensor noise, the near-critical growth-rate error is 1.8 x 10^-3 s^-1, substantially lower than with standard DMD without delay embedding. A five-state real reduced-order model is formed from the HODMD subspace, and its flap-input matrix is estimated from a small-amplitude PRBS record using DMDc. For an independent chirp input, the normalized error over all channels is 2.4 x 10^-3. The constrained MPC stabilizes the true post-critical plant for an initial pitch perturbation of 8 degrees with a flap limit of 1 degree, whereas saturated LQR designed from the same model reaches the prescribed validity limit. Three supporting studies assess transferability. SU2 simulations show HODMD frequency recovery consistent with the available spectral resolution; OpenFOAM dynamic-mesh calculations show nearly linear articulated-flap moment authority from 2 to 8 degrees with frequency-dependent gain; and a two-way SU2 Python-FSI case demonstrates bounded disturbance rejection using a proportional-derivative baseline. These studies support modal identification, actuator authority, and closed-loop feasibility, but are not presented as CFD-level MPC validation. The framework provides a reproducible route from early-time measurements to constrained aeroelastic control.
tldr: An interpretable data-driven framework combining HODMD, DMDc, and constrained MPC for actuator-limited flutter suppression in a pitch-plunge aeroelastic typical section.
motivation: Flutter is a dangerous aeroelastic instability that requires reliable active suppression under tight actuator constraints, motivating model-based control derived directly from measured data.
method: Higher-order DMD identifies dominant frequencies and growth rates from four noisy structural channels, DMDc estimates the flap-input matrix from a PRBS record, and the resulting five-state reduced model feeds a constrained MPC controller; SU2, OpenFOAM, and FSI studies assess transferability.
result: With 2% RMS sensor noise the near-critical growth-rate error is 1.8e-3 s^-1, the chirp-input normalized error is 2.4e-3, and the constrained MPC stabilizes the post-critical plant for an 8-degree pitch perturbation under a 1-degree flap limit where saturated LQR fails.
conclusion: The work offers a reproducible measurement-to-control pipeline for constrained aeroelastic flutter suppression, though the CFD/FSI studies support only modal identification and feasibility rather than full CFD-level MPC validation.

title: Fast Relax-and-Round Unit Commitment With Topological Constraints
authors: Evan J. R. Brody, Charles Foltz, Eve Tsybina, Slaven Peles, Shaked Regev
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent developments in the US knowledge economy have created a significant growth in datacenter loads, with two major consequences for power generation. First, to compensate for growth in load, datacenters are encouraged to bring their own generating units. Second, in search of the remaining pools of dispatchable generation, utilities are increasingly turning to subtransmission and distribution level generating assets. Coupled with increasing loads and the resulting tighter grid conditions, both trends are likely to create a need to commit a large number of localized generating units under grid constraints. We propose an extension of Relax-and- Round Unit Commitment (RRUC) that is capable of committing generating units for larger problems faster than conventional methods, while staying within intertemporal and spatial MVA constraints. We demonstrate the performance of RRUC using synthetic congestible test systems ranging from 100 to 20,000 buses. RRUC consistently finds low cost solutions, independent of the problem size, and its run time increases sub-quadratically in the number of buses. RRUC can solve the 100 bus system in less than a second and the 20,000 bus system 7 minutes. In contrast, a leading state of the art solver cannot find a feasible solution to the 100 bus system in 15 minutes.
tldr: The paper presents an extended Relax-and-Round Unit Commitment (RRUC) algorithm that commits many localized generating units under intertemporal and spatial MVA grid constraints far faster than state-of-the-art solvers.
motivation: Growth in datacenter loads is driving utilities to enlist distributed, subtransmission-level generating assets, creating a need to solve large-scale unit commitment problems under tighter grid constraints that conventional solvers handle poorly.
method: The authors extend the Relax-and-Round Unit Commitment heuristic to incorporate intertemporal and spatial MVA constraints, then benchmark it on synthetic congestible test systems ranging from 100 to 20,000 buses.
result: RRUC finds low-cost solutions with runtime growing sub-quadratically in the number of buses, solving a 100-bus system in under a second and a 20,000-bus system in about 7 minutes, whereas a leading solver fails to find any feasible solution to the 100-bus case within 15 minutes.
conclusion: RRUC offers a scalable and robust approach to constrained unit commitment for modern power grids, though the work is a classical power-systems optimization contribution with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, or quantum networks.

title: A Family Of Spectral Conjugate Gradient Algorithms Derived By Least-squares Approximations Based On A Modified quasi--Newton Update With Application To A Revised Robust Binary Classification Model
authors: Saman Babaie-Kafaki, Maryam Khoshsimaye-Bargard, Ahmad Mousavi
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13526v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a spectral three-term modification of the classic Hestenes--Stiefel conjugate gradient algorithm, preserving its anti-jamming characteristic and, simultaneously, taking care of the sufficient descent property. We discuss how a modified secant equation can be extracted from our modification scheme, yielding a memoryless BFGS updating formula. Then, the spectral parameter of our method is obtained by steering its direction toward the given BFGS direction within a least-squares context. Using our technical improvements, we outline the general framework of our algorithm and discuss its theoretical features, including the descent and convergence properties, without the convexity assumption. We put our algorithm to the test in comparison with the three other conjugate gradient algorithms on a set of CUTEr unconstrained optimization test models, comparing the outputs using the Dolan--More measure. Next, we provide a concise evaluation of the results, highlighting the practical advantages of our algorithm. As a real-world case study, we introduce a reduced quadratic surface SVM with the rescaled loss for robust binary classification and apply the proposed algorithm to assess its accuracy and training time against several other SVMs.
tldr: The paper develops a spectral three-term conjugate gradient algorithm based on least-squares approximations to a modified quasi-Newton (BFGS) update and applies it to a reduced quadratic-surface SVM model for robust binary classification.
motivation: Classical conjugate gradient methods can suffer from jamming and lack guaranteed sufficient descent, and the authors aim to combine anti-jamming behavior with descent guarantees while also demonstrating practical utility in a machine learning classification setting.
method: A modified secant equation is derived to yield a memoryless BFGS update, and the spectral parameter is chosen by steering the search direction toward the BFGS direction via a least-squares approximation; convergence without convexity assumptions is analyzed, and numerical tests use CUTEr benchmarks and a rescaled-loss SVM classifier.
result: The proposed algorithm is benchmarked against three other conjugate gradient methods using Dolan-Moré performance profiles and applied to the SVM model to compare accuracy and training time against several other SVM variants.
conclusion: The spectral conjugate gradient framework offers theoretical descent and convergence properties and shows practical advantages in both unconstrained optimization benchmarks and robust binary classification.

title: Domain Splitting With Localized Implicit Prediction For Wave Equations
authors: Roland Maier Tim Buchholz
abstract: ArXiv:2609.13822v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose and analyze a non-iterative domain decomposition time integrator for the linear acoustic wave equation. The method is based on an overlapping decomposition in space and uses a localized implicit prediction to provide artificial boundary data at the interfaces. We use conforming finite elements of arbitrary order to discretize in space and allow spatially varying material coefficients. We prove an error bound relative to the global Crank--Nicolson approximation that decays exponentially with the size of both the subdomain and prediction overlaps. Compared to earlier work, this new method avoids a CFL-type step size restriction and allows the use of finite elements of arbitrary order. The analysis combines a discrete Saint-Venant principle with new decay and truncation estimates for the localized prediction. Numerical experiments support the analysis and demonstrate stable behavior for all tested time step sizes, accuracy comparable to that of the global Crank--Nicolson approximation, and the potential for efficient parallel execution.
tldr: The paper proposes a non-iterative overlapping domain decomposition time integrator for the linear acoustic wave equation, using localized implicit prediction to supply artificial interface data, with finite elements of arbitrary order and provable exponential error decay.
motivation: Global implicit time integration of wave equations is computationally expensive, while explicit schemes suffer CFL-type step-size restrictions; a stable, non-iterative domain decomposition method could enable efficient parallel computation without these constraints.
method: The authors use a spatial overlapping domain decomposition with conforming finite elements of arbitrary order and a localized implicit prediction providing artificial boundary data, analyzing error via a discrete Saint-Venant principle plus new decay and truncation estimates.
